title: documents strict: bare Yandex Cloud keys, Latin names under personal keys and in English prose stay
body:
Found on `main` after #121 (and on 0.19.0) with `profile: 'documents'`, `properNames: 'capitalized'`, `strict: true`. All values below are synthetic.

```js
import { createSyncSanitizer } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const policy = { profile: 'documents', properNames: 'capitalized', strict: true };
const text = createSyncSanitizer(policy);
const json = createSyncSanitizer({ ...policy, structured: 'json' });
```

`X40` below stands for 40 mixed-case token characters such as `aB3_xY9kaB3_xY9k…`.

## 1. Bare Yandex Cloud credentials stay

| input | output | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AQVN` + 36 token chars (API key) | unchanged | replaced |
| `key AQVN` + 36 token chars | unchanged | replaced |
| `t1.` + payload + `.` + 86 token chars (IAM token) | unchanged | replaced |
| `YCAJE` + 20 token chars (static key id) | unchanged | replaced |
| `YC` + 38 token chars (static key secret) | unchanged | replaced |

With a label such as `Authorization: Api-Key …` or `iam_token=…` they are replaced. The prefixes are documented and fixed, like `sk-ant-` or `ghp_`, which are already recognized bare.

## 2. One Latin word, a Latin file name or a number under a personal key stays (`structured: 'json'`)

| input | output | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{"candidateName":"Petrov"}` | unchanged | value replaced |
| `{"candidate_name":"Petrov"}` | unchanged | value replaced |
| `{"displayName":"Petrov"}` | unchanged | value replaced |
| `{"originalFileName":"Petrov_Ivan_CV.pdf"}` | unchanged | value replaced |
| `{"age":34}` | unchanged | value replaced |
| `{"birthYear":1991}` | unchanged | value replaced |

`{"candidateName":"Петров"}` gives `{"candidateName":"[REDACTED]"}`, so only the Latin form is missing. `vocabulary.personalFields` holds `firstname`, `lastname`, `middlename` and `patronymic`. Compound keys that end in `name` (`candidateName`, `displayName`, `fullName`), `age` and `birthYear` look like they belong to the same group. A bare `name` is ambiguous (it also names jobs and products), so it can stay.

## 3. Latin names in English prose stay

| input | output | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `candidate Ivan replied` | unchanged | `candidate [REDACTED] replied` |
| `Dear John,` | unchanged | `Dear [REDACTED],` |
| `Mr. Brown called` | unchanged | `Mr. [REDACTED] called` |
| `message from Ivan: ok` | unchanged | `message from [REDACTED]: ok` |

`Ivan Petrov replied` gives `[REDACTED] replied`, so two words are caught and one is not. `scripts: ['Cyrillic', 'Latin']` catches these, but it also replaces ordinary capitalized English words: `Request Failed: POST /api` gives `[REDACTED] Failed: [REDACTED] /api`. The optional `/ner` recognizer does not catch the single-word forms either. A person cue before a capitalized Latin word (`candidate`, `recruiter`, `applicant`, `Dear`, `Hi`, `Mr`, `Ms`, `Dr`) would cover the first three without the Latin script's false positives.

## Expected

Each row replaced, with tests, and English text without a person cue left as it is (`Request Failed: POST /api`, `Candidate Stage changed`).

title: fix: protect strict document values and preserve work durations
body:
With `profile: 'documents'`, `properNames: 'capitalized'` and `strict: true`, obfuscated emails and military IDs could retain sensitive fragments, lowercase employers and Cyrillic names before colons remained visible, and work durations were redacted as ages. This change fixes every reported row in text, JSON and JSONL.

- Extend the existing bounded email separator grammar with bracketed English/Russian dot forms. Preserve complete contact and identifier findings when proper-name matches cover only a domain or ID series.
- Recognize lowercase employers after explicit Russian employment cues. Replace unknown capitalized Cyrillic words before colons in activated prose while preserving known labels, English labels and JSON keys.
- Preserve clause-local work durations and parenthesized known-technology durations in strict mode; keep explicit ages and bare strict ages sensitive. Retain stable repeated redaction and duration context through custom placeholders and generated fake values.
- Add value-free overlap counts through the existing optional debug callback, update API/coverage documentation and include a patch Changeset for the automated release.

Reproduce with `createSyncSanitizer({ profile: 'documents', properNames: 'capitalized', strict: true }).sanitize(input).text`. Previously `ivan собака example.org` became `ivan собака [REDACTED]`, and `военный билет АБ 1234567` kept its number. Both now replace the complete sensitive value. `Стаж: 5 лет` and `работал там 5 лет` stay unchanged; `Kubernetes (5 лет)` becomes `[REDACTED] (5 лет)`. `кандидату 34 года`, `мне 34 года` and `возраст 41` remain protected.

Verification:

- The initial regression suite failed 48/65 cases on `e762a22`, including all ten reported rows in each of three formats. The final issue suite passes 77/77 cases, covering both sync/async APIs, exact source spans, idempotence, escaped JSON keys/values, restoration, duration boundaries (including multiword Power BI), custom placeholders, fake values and diagnostics.
- A focused five-file compatibility run passes 502 tests, including existing document/strict catalogs, issue-87 duration controls, structural prose, streaming, bounded file workers and CLI behavior. Later focused checks pass all 84 existing issue-100 document tests and all 84 combined issue-120/placeholder-residual tests.
- Focused ESLint passes with zero warnings. Changed files pass Prettier and the committed Changeset passes validation.
- CI initially exposed accidental matching of the cue `компании` (Ubuntu Node job log lines 4286/4299) and resulting placeholder shifts (lines 4312/4324). The cue is now preserved and the existing regression tests pass. Full validation on source commit `124cd8e` is green: 52 checks passed; 10 inapplicable release/deployment jobs were skipped. [Node/Bun/Deno on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS, plus lint, documentation and release guards](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42616017906), [web/desktop application checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42616017724), [security scans and audits](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42616017694), and [link checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42616017658) all passed.

Final documentation commit `c5371ca` also passes all four workflows: 23 checks passed; 18 inapplicable or unchanged-code checks were skipped. Source and tests are identical to the fully tested `124cd8e` commit. [Final commit checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/pull/121/checks).

```sh
node --max-old-space-size=384 --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-timeout=30000 tests/sanitizer-issue-120.test.js
```

[Requirement mapping and before/after evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-120-75801fa5c894/experiments/issue-120/README.md). The older issue-106 preservation expectation for `Ромашка: менеджер` is updated because this issue explicitly requests that behavior to change. Colon handling is limited to Cyrillic words in activated prose; lowercase employers require employment context and skill-duration disambiguation uses the existing finite technology vocabulary.

Fixes #120

title: 0.19.0 strict: obfuscated emails, military ID numbers and lowercase employers stay; durations replaced as ages
body:
Found on 0.19.0 with `profile: 'documents'`, `properNames: 'capitalized'`, `strict: true` (plain text and `structured: 'json'` give the same results). All values below are synthetic.

```js
import { createSyncSanitizer } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const s = createSyncSanitizer({ profile: 'documents', properNames: 'capitalized', strict: true });
s.sanitize(input).text;
```

## Kept (false negatives)

| input | output | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ivan [at] example [dot] org` | unchanged | the address replaced |
| `ivan (at) example (dot) org` | unchanged | the address replaced |
| `ivan собака example.org` | `ivan собака [REDACTED]` | the local part replaced too |
| `пишите ivan[at]example.org` | `пишите ivan[at][REDACTED]` | the local part replaced too |
| `военный билет АБ 1234567` | `военный билет [REDACTED] 1234567` | the number replaced (the series alone is replaced now) |
| `работал в ромашке три года` | unchanged | the lowercase employer after `работал в` replaced |
| `Ромашка: менеджер` | unchanged | a capitalized Cyrillic word before a colon replaced when the text holds data and the word is not a known label (`Опыт`, `Стаж`, ...) |

`ivan at example dot org` is replaced, so the bracketed and `собака` forms look like missing variants of the same rule.

## Replaced (false positives under `strict`)

Without `strict` these durations stay, as fixed in #87. With `strict` they are replaced as ages:

| input | output | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Стаж: 5 лет` | `Стаж: [REDACTED]` | unchanged |
| `работал там 5 лет` | `работал там [REDACTED]` | unchanged |
| `Kubernetes (5 лет)` | `[REDACTED] ([REDACTED])` | `[REDACTED] (5 лет)` (the capitalized word is expected with `properNames`) |

`опыт работы 10 лет` stays under `strict`, so a duration cue (`стаж`, `работал`, a parenthesised skill) could take the same path. An age stays replaced: `кандидату 34 года`, `мне 34 года`, `возраст 41`.

## Expected

The kept forms replaced and the durations left as they are under `strict`, with tests for each row.

title: feat: add configurable synchronous sanitization and offline document recognition
body:
Synchronous log hooks previously ignored custom detectors, document policies could not be tuned, and several reported personal-data formats remained visible. This PR implements all ten subissues of #118 in one change: synchronous detectors, rule/type/field controls, configurable vocabulary, structured selectors, verified callback transforms, compiled known values, optional offline recognition, expanded document formats and an opt-in strict policy.

- Reuse existing normalized/decoded/JSON offset mapping in both engines; reject sync thenables and fail closed on callback errors. Expose `createSyncSanitizer` and complete TypeScript declarations.
- Publish stable rule ids, guard credential disabling, add field-content scan policy and additive/per-list replacement vocabulary. Preserve defaults outside the requested catalog improvements.
- Support exact/dotted/wildcard sensitive/allowed fields while preserving structured formatting, keys and numeric primitives. Keep callbacks in stream/file coordinators; restore compiled metadata inside workers.
- Load the optional `@nlpjs/ner` peer only through `/ner`. Recognition is symbolic, synchronous after initialization and fully offline. Publish exact-span precision/recall by type/language, all six issue examples, benign controls, challenge misses and per-KiB cost. It is a finite recognizer, not a claim of universal NER.
- Add a minor release Changeset, runnable policy example, API/rule reference and coverage documentation.

The [complete requirement inventory, alternatives, root causes and verification mapping](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-118-bfb692598f84/docs/case-studies/issue-118/README.md) covers every issue and original row. Research compared Presidio, Transformers.js/ONNX and NLP.js; the selected component preserves the synchronous and optional-loading contract.

Reproduce the original catalog problems with the checked-in fixtures: `тел.: 1234567`, `anna(собака)example(точка)org`, `Компания - Ромашка`, and the other issue rows. The catalog suite fails 92/115 cases on baseline `db4f228`. Focused verification covers 527 passing cases, including the expanded strict vocabulary and integration checks; all CI checks pass on final commit `af88fae`: [full runtime matrix](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42176509272), [security](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42176509037), [desktop example packaging](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42176509056), and [links](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42176509178).

```sh
node --max-old-space-size=384 --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-timeout=30000 tests/sanitizer-issue-118-*.test.js tests/sanitizer-document-entities.test.js tests/sanitizer-issue-100.test.js tests/package-metadata.test.js

```

Tests compare exact text/JSON/JSONL output in both engines, each issue control, failure behavior, callback escaping/leakage, immutable compilation, CLI configuration and stream/file paths. Integration review preserved the existing built-in transformation semantics, tightened custom vocabulary spans, and fixed both CodeQL URL-normalization findings with linear scans and a retained bounded probe. Three older preservation expectations were updated because the requested employer/address coverage deliberately supersedes them. The [bounded measurements](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-118-bfb692598f84/docs/case-studies/issue-118/measurements.json) report 3.30 ms per KiB with 500 compiled known values versus 2.80 ms without a list (0.73 ms direct matching); optional recognition costs 0.0434 ms/KiB. These are illustrative synthetic measurements. Ambiguous bare-name limits and strict-policy over-redaction tradeoffs are documented explicitly.

## Summary

A second synthetic catalog on 0.17.1. It adds to #104, which covers employers in dated lines, comma phones and school forms. #105 asks for an opt-in rule on capitalized words: these rows should be handled by the profile itself wherever a cue or a shape allows it, so that the opt-in rule catches less.

### Names (a patronymic, initials, mixed scripts and given names outside the built-in list)

### Addresses and regions

### Citizenship with no label

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `гражданство РФ` | `гражданство РФ` |
| `гражданин Беларуси` | `гражданин Беларуси` |

### Vehicle plates

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `госномер А123ВС77` | `госномер А123ВС77` |
| `А123ВС 77 RUS` | `А123ВС 77 RUS` |

### Organizations

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `Компания - Ромашка` | `Компания - Ромашка` |
| `Место работы — Ромашка` | `Место работы — Ромашка` |

### Schools and courses

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `МГУ` | `МГУ` |
| `МГУ им. Ломоносова` | `МГУ им. Ломоносова` |
| `ТГУ, 2012` | `ТГУ, 2012` |
| `бакалавр, ТГУ` | `бакалавр, ТГУ` |

| `Курсы Лютик` | `Курсы Лютик` |
| `курс на Ромашке` | `курс на Ромашке` |

## Cues a rule can use

- `Ивановна`: a patronymic ending, on its own, is close to a name by shape.
- `СМИРНОВА А.В.`: `Смирнова А. В.` is replaced, so only the uppercase form is missed.
- `Aннa Cмирнoвa`: Latin letters inside Cyrillic words. Normalizing lookalikes before matching catches it, and a mixed-script word is unusual in itself.
- `ул` with no dot, `пр-т`, `шоссе`, `область`, `район`: street and region words. `Москва, ул. Тверская, 5` shows the gap: the city goes and the street and number stay.
- `гражданство`, `гражданин`: the same word with a colon is a label already.
- A plate has a fixed letter and digit shape, and `госномер` is a cue.
- `Компания -`, `Место работы —`, `Банк`, `Группа`, `стартап`, `менеджер в`: cue words next to a capitalized word.
- `им.`, `диплом`, `бакалавр`, `колледж`, `курсы`: school cues. An uppercase acronym with one of these, or with a year after a comma, is enough.

Bare words with no cue, such as `Смирнова`, `Сергей` or `Питер`, need a wider list, the option in #105 or an in-process recognizer. They're listed so the docs can state what the profile does and doesn't cover.

## Minor over-replacement

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ОГРНИП` | `[REDACTED]` | unchanged, as it's a label with no value |
| `Romashka Inc.` | `[REDACTED].` | same output, or the dot goes with the name as in `ООО Ромашка.` |

## Must stay unchanged

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `Использовал Kubernetes и PostgreSQL` | `Использовал Kubernetes и PostgreSQL` |
| `Встреча в понедельник` | `Встреча в понедельник` |
| `Группа разработки выросла` | `Группа разработки выросла` |
| `Менеджер по продажам` | `Менеджер по продажам` |
| `Курсы повышения квалификации` | `Курсы повышения квалификации` |
| `улица была закрыта` | `улица была закрыта` |
| `Банк данных обновлён` | `Банк данных обновлён` |

## Acceptance

- Every row with a cue is replaced, and every control keeps its output.
- `docs/COVERAGE.md` lists the forms that stay on purpose.

title: Strict profile for sensitive attributes and ambiguous bare values
body:
## Problem

These stay on 0.17.1, and a default profile is right to be careful, because each is ambiguous without context. Stored logs need the opposite tradeoff, where losing a date is cheap and keeping a person's data is not.

### Sensitive attributes with no label

- `женщина`
- `мужчина`
- `замужем`
- `женат, двое детей`
- `двое детей`
- `русская`
- `православный`
- `инвалидность 2 группы`
- `беременна`
- `судимость погашена`
- `член партии`

Labelled forms already work: `Пол: женский` gives `Пол: [REDACTED]` and `национальность: татарин` gives `национальность: [REDACTED]`.

### Bare values with no label

- `34 года`
- `12.03.1991`
- `12 марта 1991`
- `1991-03-12`
- `45 10 123456`
- `4510123456`
- `9161234567`
- `125009`

## Expected

An opt-in profile or option for stored logs, for example `profile: 'documents', strict: true`. Under it, these are replaced:

- health, religion, ethnicity, criminal record, political and family attributes, in Russian and English, in their common word forms;
- standalone ages, calendar dates in prose, passport-shaped and phone-shaped digit groups, and postal codes.

Dates and numbers in structural positions stay. That means ISO timestamps with a time part, values under fields declared with `structuralFields`, and numeric JSON values.

## Must stay under the strict option

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `опыт работы 10 лет` | `опыт работы 10 лет` |
| `Стаж 5 лет` | `Стаж 5 лет` |
| `2026-01-15T10:30:00.000Z` | `2026-01-15T10:30:00.000Z` |
| `request took 9161234567 ns` | `request took 9161234567 ns` |
| `Дети: нет` | `Дети: нет` |

`опыт работы 10 лет` shows the hard case: a duration and an age have the same shape. If it can't be separated reliably, the docs should say which way the option goes.

## Acceptance

- With the option on, every listed row is replaced and every control stays.
- With it off, nothing changes.

title: documents profile: forms that stay though they have a label or shape
body:
## Summary

A wide synthetic catalog on 0.17.1. Each row below stays unchanged, and each has a cue or a shape a rule can use. All values are synthetic.

### Contact details

- `тел.: 1234567`
- `8 9 1 6 1 2 3 4 5 6 7`
- `anna(собака)example(точка)org`
- `a n n a @ example . org`
- `discord: anna#1234`
- `max: anna_s`

### Profile and personal links

- `ok.ru/profile/123456`
- `gitlab.com/anna-s`
- `habr.com/ru/users/anna_s`
- `facebook.com/anna.s`
- `https://example.org/cv/abc123def`
- `https://example.org/~anna/`
- `https://anna.example.org/cv.pdf`

### Labelled dates and ages

- `д.р. 12/03/91`
- `день рождения 5 мая`
- `34 y.o.`
- `45 лет от роду`

### Labelled and checksum-valid identifiers

- `военный билет АБ 1234567`
- `VIN WVWZZZ1JZXW000001`

### Organizations and schools

- `ооо ромашка`
- `Romashka, manager`
- `at Romashka`
- `graduated from MSU`
- `MIT, 2012`

### Encoded values

- `anna%40example.org`
- `https://x.example/?m=anna%40example.org`
- `YW5uYUBleGFtcGxlLm9yZw==`

## Why these matter

- `тел.:` is a label, so a seven-digit local number shouldn't need more evidence.
- `д.р.` and `день рождения` are labels already known in other forms: `DOB: 1991-03-12` and `родилась 12.03.1991` are replaced.
- `anna at example dot org` and `anna[at]example.org` are replaced, while `(собака)` with `(точка)` is not.
- `ООО Ромашка` is replaced, while the same text in lowercase is not. A legal form is a strong cue in any case.
- A base64 name is decoded and replaced, while a base64 email is not, and neither is a percent-encoded email, in a link or out of one.

## Must stay unchanged

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `опыт работы 10 лет` | `опыт работы 10 лет` |
| `Стаж 5 лет` | `Стаж 5 лет` |
| `order 89161234567 shipped` | `order 89161234567 shipped` |
| `id 79161234567` | `id 79161234567` |
| `Connection to Postgres lost, retrying` | `Connection to Postgres lost, retrying` |
| `commit 9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706f5e4d3c2b1a098765432` | `commit 9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706f5e4d3c2b1a098765432` |
| `listening on 0.0.0.0:3000` | `listening on 0.0.0.0:3000` |
| `at parse (/srv/app/dist/a.js:10:3)` | `at parse (/srv/app/dist/a.js:10:3)` |

## Acceptance

Every listed row is replaced, and every control keeps its output.

title: Reusable compiled known values for per-record use
body:
## Problem

`knownPersonal` is the most reliable route to high coverage, because it matches the value rather than its shape. It's case-insensitive and handles Russian forms:

| Known value | Type | Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Ромашка` | ORGANIZATION | `работал в ромашка` | `работал в [REDACTED]` |
| `Ромашка` | ORGANIZATION | `работал в Ромашке` | `работал в [REDACTED]` |
| `Ромашка` | ORGANIZATION | `Ромашка: менеджер` | `[REDACTED]: менеджер` |
| `МГУ` | EDUCATION | `окончил мгу` | `окончил [REDACTED]` |
| `Тверь` | LOCATION | `Живу в Твери` | `Живу в [REDACTED]` |

Using it in a log path means passing a list for each record or request, and the cost grows with the list on every call. On a 1 KB line on one laptop, with no other tuning: no list about 8.9 ms, 10 values 9.4 ms, 30 values 10.2 ms, 100 values 13.6 ms, 500 values 67 ms. The tail is what makes larger lists impractical on a hot path.

There's also no documented answer to two questions:

- Which `type` values change behaviour? Any uppercase string appears to be accepted.
- Which values match across formats? A date and a phone number do. A link only matches with its scheme: with `https://example.org/anna` known, `example.org/anna` gives `example.org/anna`, and `https://example.org/anna?x=1` gives `[REDACTED]?x=1`.

## Expected

```js
const known = compileKnown([{ type: 'ORGANIZATION', value: 'Ромашка' }]);
sanitize(line, { profile: 'documents', knownPersonal: known });
```

- A compiled list can be reused and merged, and it doesn't hold anything beyond what the caller passed.
- `docs/API.md` lists the types and what each one matches, across formats and word forms.

## Acceptance

- With a compiled list of 500 values, cost per call stays within 10% of no list, plus the matching itself.
- A known link also matches without its scheme, and its query string and trailing slash are replaced with it.
- Output is the same as with a plain array.

title: Offline in-process recognition for names with no cue
body:
## Problem

Pattern rules can't recognize an organization, school or place with no cue, and `minConfidence` doesn't help, because `inspect` returns no finding at all for these:

- `Работал в Ромашке менеджером.`: output unchanged, also with `minConfidence: 0`, inspect finds 0
- `Ромашка: менеджер, 3 года.`: output unchanged, also with `minConfidence: 0`, inspect finds 0
- `Worked at Romashka for three years.`: output unchanged, also with `minConfidence: 0`, inspect finds 0
- `graduated from MSU`: output unchanged, also with `minConfidence: 0`, inspect finds 0
- `MIT, 2012`: output unchanged, also with `minConfidence: 0`, inspect finds 0
- `at Romashka`: output unchanged, also with `minConfidence: 0`, inspect finds 0

`docs/COVERAGE.md` points to the Presidio bridge for this. It's a subprocess with a Python model, so it can't run in a synchronous log hook and is a heavy dependency for a JavaScript service.

## Expected

An optional, offline, in-process recognizer for person, organization, school and location names in Russian and English, for example a small ONNX or WASM model loaded by a separate entry point:

```js
import { createNerDetector } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/ner';
const detector = await createNerDetector({ languages: ['ru', 'en'] });
```

- It's a separate optional dependency, with no download at analysis time.
- Once loaded it can run synchronously, or the docs state how to run it from a worker when it can't.
- `docs/COVERAGE.md` publishes precision and recall per type and language, with the test set.

## Acceptance

- The rows above are replaced with the detector on.
- `Использовал Kubernetes и PostgreSQL`, `Встреча в понедельник` and operational English stay.
- Cost per kilobyte is published. With the detector off, nothing changes in size or speed.

title: Custom transformation callback and a synchronous engine interface
body:
## Problem

Replacements come from a closed list of modes:

```js
sanitize('Анна Смирнова', { profile: 'documents', transformation: (finding) => 'Z' });
// throws ERR_CONFIG
```

The stream and outbound APIs accept a custom `sanitizer`, which is a clean way to swap the engine. Both are async, and `sanitize()` has no equivalent, so swapping an implementation in a synchronous path means rebuilding it around the library.

The stages are partly there already. `inspect()` detects, `redact()` replaces with no verification, and `knownOnly` with `findings` replaces with verification:

```js
sanitize('Ромашка, Анна Смирнова, a@b.example', { profile: 'documents', knownOnly: true, findings: [{ start: 0, end: 7, category: 'personal', type: 'ORGANIZATION', rule: 'x' }] }).text;
// "[REDACTED], Анна Смирнова, a@b.example"
```

The `knownOnly` row in `docs/API.md` mentions known values and reused maps but not `findings`, so this isn't described as a supported way to replace detection.

## Expected

1. `transformation` and `transformations[type]` accept a function `(finding) => string`. The result goes through residual verification, and a throw blocks output.
2. Documented stages, each with a stated contract: detect, merge, transform, verify.
3. A `SyncSanitizer` interface with `inspect` and `sanitize`, plus a documented recipe for replacing detection while keeping verification.

## Acceptance

- A function transformation works in text and structured modes, and a result that still holds the original value is blocked.
- Passing a Promise-returning function throws `ERR_CONFIG` in synchronous calls.
- Existing modes don't change.

title: sensitiveFields: case styles, nested paths and an allow-list mode
body:
## Problem

`sensitiveFields` only matches one exact spelling at any depth, while built-in personal field names match in any case style.

| Input | `sensitiveFields` | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{"fooBar":"Значение"}` | `["fooBar"]` | `{"fooBar":"[REDACTED]"}` |
| `{"foo_bar":"Значение"}` | `["fooBar"]` | `{"foo_bar":"Значение"}` |
| `{"FooBar":"Значение"}` | `["fooBar"]` | `{"FooBar":"Значение"}` |
| `{"fooBar":"Значение"}` | `["foobar"]` | `{"fooBar":"Значение"}` |
| `{"a":{"b":"Значение"}}` | `["a.b"]` | `{"a":{"b":"Значение"}}` |
| `{"x":"Значение"}` | `["*"]` | `{"x":"Значение"}` |

A value logged alone under a neutral key has nothing to recognize, whatever the detectors do:

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `{"note":"1991-03-12"}` | `{"note":"1991-03-12"}` |
| `{"note":"Romashka"}` | `{"note":"Romashka"}` |
| `{"note":"https://example.org/cv/abc123def"}` | `{"note":"https://example.org/cv/abc123def"}` |

The only complete answer for such values is to name the fields that are safe to keep.

## Expected

1. Names match in any case style by default, the same as built-in field names. `exactFields` keeps today's behaviour.
2. Dotted paths and `*` work: `a.b`, `items.*.name`.
3. A new option, `allowedFields`: in JSON and JSONL, string values under any other key become `[REDACTED]`. Values under listed keys are still scanned. Numbers and booleans are unaffected.

## Acceptance

- The table rows behave as above.
- `allowedFields: ['msg', 'level']` on `{"msg":"ok","note":"Romashka"}` gives `{"msg":"ok","note":"[REDACTED]"}`.
- Output stays valid JSON with the same keys and numbers.

title: Let callers extend the document vocabulary
body:
## Problem

The documents profile depends on closed lists: role words, organization cues, school cues, label names and personal field names. They can't be extended. `document-vocabulary.js` isn't exported, and a deep import fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. Every miss therefore needs an upstream release.

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `Маркетолог, Ромашка, Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Маркетолог, Ромашка, Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка, Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |
| `группа компаний Ромашка` | `группа компаний Ромашка` |
| `Обучение: Skillbox, 2020` | `Обучение: Skillbox, 2020` |
| `стартап Ромашка` | `стартап Ромашка` |

Only the first word of the entry decides the first two rows. A caller who knows their domain could add `маркетолог` in one line.

## Expected

```js
sanitize(text, {
  profile: 'documents',
  vocabulary: {
    roles: ['маркетолог'],
    organizationCues: ['группа компаний', 'стартап'],
    educationCues: ['обучение'],
    personalLabels: ['личный контакт'],
    personalFields: ['contactPerson'],
  },
});
```

- The additions extend the built-in lists. A `replace: true` form swaps a list out entirely.
- Bad entries throw `ERR_CONFIG`.
- Lists are normalized the same way as the built-in ones, so case and Russian word forms behave alike.
- The built-in lists are exported read-only, so a caller can see what's already covered.

## Acceptance

- With `roles: ['маркетолог']`, the first row gives the same output as the second.
- With no `vocabulary`, output doesn't change.
- The cost stays bounded, and repeated calls with the same vocabulary don't recompile it each time.

title: Per-rule and per-type control over built-in detection
body:
## Problem

Built-in rules can't be switched off or narrowed one at a time, so an over-redaction or a noisy rule has no fix on the caller's side. What exists today doesn't cover it:

| Attempt | Result on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `sanitize(s, { rules: { person: false } })` | throws ERR_CONFIG (no such option) |
| `{"location":"apps/api"}` with `structuralFields: ['location']` | `{"location":"[REDACTED]"}` |
| `Работала в компании Ромашка` with `documentEntities: false` | `Работала в компании [REDACTED]` |
| `Работала в компании Ромашка` with no options at all | `Работала в компании [REDACTED]` |

The last two rows look like a bug: `docs/API.md` says `documentEntities: false` turns document recognizers off and that they are off by default, yet this cue still fires. `Менеджер, Ромашка (2019 – 2021)` does follow the flag.

`publicEntities` can exempt one exact value, but it needs a source and a review date per value, so it doesn't suit a class of false positives such as technology names.

## Expected

- Rule ids in `Finding.rule` are documented and stable.
- `rules: { '<id>': false }` turns off one rule, and an unknown id throws `ERR_CONFIG`.
- `types: { ORGANIZATION: false }` turns off one type.
- Credential rules can't be turned off this way unless the caller also sets an explicit, separately named option.
- A way to exempt a built-in field name, for example `fields: { location: 'scan' }`, so the value is scanned as ordinary text rather than replaced whole.
- `documentEntities: false` turns off every document recognizer, or the docs say which ones stay.

## Acceptance

- Each row above has a documented way to get the opposite result.
- With no new option set, output doesn't change.

title: sanitize() accepts detectors and does nothing; allow synchronous detectors
body:
## Problem

Unknown options fail closed with `ERR_CONFIG`, so a typo can't turn protection off. `detectors` is the exception: the synchronous `sanitize()` and `inspect()` accept it and do nothing. A comment in `index.d.ts` says synchronous functions use native rules only, but the call raises no error, so a caller who misses the comment believes the detector runs.

```js
const detector = { detect: (t) => { const i = t.indexOf('Ромашка'); return i < 0 ? [] : [{ start: i, end: i + 7, category: 'personal', type: 'ORGANIZATION', rule: 'x', confidence: 1 }]; } };
sanitize('Ромашка тут', { profile: 'documents', detectors: [detector] }).text;
// "Ромашка тут"
(await createSanitizer({ profile: 'documents', detectors: [detector], secretlint: false }).sanitize('Ромашка тут')).text;
// "[REDACTED] тут"
```

A log hook has to be synchronous, so it can't use `createSanitizer`. Today the only synchronous route is to run your own detection and pass `findings` to `sanitize()`. That works, but it means every caller rebuilds the detector loop, and `structured: 'json'` needs offsets into the serialized text.

## Expected

1. `sanitize()` and `inspect()` run detectors whose `detect` returns an array, on the same inputs as the async engine, including each string value in structured mode.
2. A detector returning a Promise throws `ERR_CONFIG` in synchronous calls instead of being skipped.
3. The types and `docs/API.md` say the same.

## Acceptance

- The example above gives `[REDACTED] тут` from both engines.
- In `structured: 'json'` a detector sees decoded string values, and its offsets refer to them.
- A detector that throws blocks output, as it does in the async engine.

title: feat: broaden document detection and add opt-in structural prose redaction
body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

Dated CV entries kept complex employers whenever the title or lead-in was outside a small role vocabulary. The document profile now uses date anchors to locate arbitrary forward titles, complex employer names and successive entries. For example, `Маркетолог, Ромашка, Лютик (2019–2021)` becomes `Маркетолог, [REDACTED] (2019–2021)` in text and JSON.

The new opt-in `properNames: 'capitalized'` rule handles no-cue prose independently per string. `Работал в Ромашке менеджером по продажам.` becomes `[REDACTED] в [REDACTED] менеджером по продажам.` Operational neighbors such as `Connection to Postgres lost, retrying` stay unchanged. Activation uses configurable Unicode scripts (default Cyrillic), parenthesized date ranges, comma-separated mobiles or `/d/<id>` links. Labels, dates, paths, JSON keys and numbers are preserved by the added rule. The option is off by default.

## Complete scope

- Cover every reported dated-employer row, arbitrary unseen titles, lead-ins, comma/parenthesis/slash/legal suffixes, industry pipes and multiple entries on a line, with English parity.
- Recognize group cues with or without quotes and repeated employment-list continuations, comma-separated Russian mobile shapes in Russian/English, the four school forms, and short `/d/<id>` links at any host.
- Preserve the reported technology and negative controls, keep relative operational `location` paths, and normalize caller-sensitive field spelling for case/underscores/hyphens.
- Expose the prose option through sync/async APIs, CLI flags/configuration, worker/stream paths and TypeScript. Map escaped and nested serialized JSON leaves independently and preserve their keys and formatting.
- Add a minor release Changeset, runnable synthetic example, bounded performance probes and detailed API/coverage documentation.

The [complete requirement inventory, alternatives, research and verification mapping](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-106-e528442ca6c2/docs/case-studies/issue-106/README.md) covers #104, its follow-up comment, #105 and #106. Research considered native Unicode properties, the existing libphonenumber-js dependency, linkify-it, Compromise and Presidio. No new runtime dependency or model is required.

## Reproduction and automated verification

Run the focused regression checks:

```sh
node --max-old-space-size=384 --test --test-timeout=30000 tests/package-metadata.test.js tests/sanitizer-issue-106.test.js tests/sanitizer-prose-integration.test.js tests/sanitizer-experience-lines.test.js tests/sanitizer-issue-100.test.js tests/sanitizer-placeholders.test.js tests/sanitizer-profiles.test.js
node_modules/.bin/eslint . --max-warnings 0
```

- The original source failed 79 of the initial 95 regression cases; the final focused selection passes all 260 tests.
- Exact text/JSON/JSONL outputs, default-off behavior, repeated redaction, script gates, Unicode/escaped keys, nested serialized JSON, stable reusable placeholder maps and restoration are covered.
- Integration checks exercise CLI flags/config, split JSONL streaming and the bounded file worker. Existing profiles, experience layouts and issue-100 document behavior are included; Chinese and Arabic document entities stay protected alongside the new prose findings.
- Hostile token probes use finite 50K/100K/200K inputs under a 128 MiB heap, 1 MiB stack and two-second matching deadline. An illustrative seven-shape run took 175 ms total. The whole-pipeline 267-byte/9-KB comparison showed similar latency before and after; no universal speedup is claimed.
- Full ESLint with zero warnings, changed-file formatting and the runnable example pass locally. The complete Node/Bun/Deno matrix on Linux/macOS/Windows passes, together with security/CodeQL, session publication, Docker, example-app builds and link checks. See the linked verification inventory for the exact implementation SHA and passing runs.

## Deliberate limits

Lowercase dated employers remain ambiguous with the required meeting control and are explicitly documented as permitted by #104. The technology/acronym policies are finite. The opt-in uppercase rule intentionally also removes ordinary capitalized words; lowercase names, labels and untriggered English prose/site roots remain as described in #105. Existing credential/explicit-sensitive policies still apply to all strings. Placeholder namespace collision protection remains enforced. The fixed-pass cost claim concerns the new scanner, not external engines or every preexisting rule.

Fixes #106
Fixes #104
Fixes #105

title: Option to replace proper names in prose that has no cue
body:
## Problem

The `documents` profile recognises organizations, schools and places by cues. Prose with no cue keeps them, and no list of cues can cover it:

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `Работал в Ромашке менеджером по продажам.` | `Работал в Ромашке менеджером по продажам.` |
| `Ромашка: менеджер, 3 года.` | `Ромашка: менеджер, 3 года.` |
| `Сотрудник работал в Romashka три года.` | `Сотрудник работал в Romashka три года.` |
| `Живу в Твери` | `Живу в Твери` |

This matters most for stored logs, where text is kept only for diagnosis and losing a few extra words costs little. Generated text that quotes a document is the worst case: on a private set of CV-shaped documents, a caller-side rule took kept organization names from 57% to under 1% in generated prose, and from 26% to 2% in the documents themselves.

## Request

An option that replaces anything shaped like a proper name, in text that a caller marks as prose. For example:

```js
sanitize(text, { profile: "documents", properNames: "capitalized" });
```

## Suggested behaviour

The rule that gave those numbers, as a starting point. It is structural and has no word lists.

Apply it to a string value only when the value holds data, meaning any of:

- a letter from a script other than the caller's operational language (a `scripts: ["Cyrillic"]` setting, for example)
- a parenthesized date range
- a comma-separated mobile number
- a link with a `/d/<id>` path

Then replace:

- any word with an uppercase letter anywhere in it, including joined forms such as `Санкт-Петербург` or `A.B`
- text in typographic quotes, such as `«ромашка лютик»`
- links, including a bare `example.org/path`
- bare mobile numbers

Keep:

- `Label:`, meaning a capitalized word right before a colon
- lowercase words, numbers and dates
- path segments and JSON keys
- values that do not hold data, byte for byte

| Input | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `Работал в Ромашке менеджером по продажам.` | `[REDACTED] в [REDACTED] менеджером по продажам.` |
| `Опыт: работал в Ромашке 5 лет` | `Опыт: работал в [REDACTED] 5 лет` |
| `Маркетолог, ГК «ромашка лютик» (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `[REDACTED], [REDACTED] [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |
| `Founder, consultant, Romashka (2019-2021)` | `[REDACTED], consultant, [REDACTED] (2019-2021)` |
| `Connection to Postgres lost, retrying` | unchanged |
| `order 89161234567 shipped` | unchanged |
| `Window Closed (2026-01-15T10:30:00.000Z)` | unchanged |

## Known limits of the rule

- An organization written in lowercase stays.
- `Ромашка: менеджер` stays, because it looks like a label.
- An English value with no such shape stays, for example `Worked at Romashka for three years.`
- A personal website root in such a value stays, for example `https://anna-smirnova.example.org/`
- A value logged alone under a neutral key with no shape stays, for example `{"note":"Romashka"}` or `{"note":"1991-03-12"}`

## Acceptance

- The option is off by default, so existing output doesn't change.
- Running it twice gives the same result as running it once.
- JSON stays valid, with the same keys and numbers.
- Cost stays linear in input length, including long tokens with no spaces.

title: documents profile 0.17.0: employers stay in dated lines with unlisted titles or a lead-in; comma phones and school forms
body:
## Summary

Checked 0.17.0 from npm after #94 and #91 closed. Everything reported there is fixed or documented, thank you. The forms below still leave personal data in text mode and in `structured: 'json'`. On a private set of CVs, employers in dated experience lines are most of what is still kept, and the kept rate did not change between 0.16.2 and 0.17.0. All values here are invented.

```js
const text = (s) => sanitize(s, { profile: 'documents' }).text;
```

## Dated experience lines

### 1. The title has to start with a listed word

`role` in `src/document-extras.js` lists 12 words. A line with the same structure is handled only if its title starts with one of them, while the date range is what anchors the entry:

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Менеджер, Ромашка, Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |
| `Маркетолог, Ромашка, Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка (Лютик) (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |
| `Маркетолог, Ромашка (Лютик) (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Romashka, LLC (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |
| `Маркетолог, Romashka, LLC (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Маркетолог, Ромашка / Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Основатель, консультант, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Маркетолог (B2B), Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |

### 2. Text before the entry

`role.test(parts[0])` is anchored to the start of the prefix, so a lead-in such as `Опыт:` stops a listed title from matching:

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Опыт: директор, основатель, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Опыт работы: Менеджер, консультант, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Опыт: менеджер (b2b), Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Стаж = 5 лет: Менеджер, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `= 3 года, Менеджер, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01). Директор, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01). Директор, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |

### 3. Other employer shapes

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Менеджер, Ромашка \| маркетинг, продажи (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка Лютик \| IT, связь (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Маркетолог, ГК «Ромашка Лютик» (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `ГК «Ромашка» (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |

## Bare mobile number after a comma

`контакт: 89161234567` is now replaced. These are not:

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Анна, 89161234567` | unchanged |
| `Письмо, 89161234567, жду ответа` | unchanged |
| `Иванова А., 79161234567, Москва` | `[REDACTED], 79161234567, [REDACTED]` |

## School acronyms and names after brackets or other cues

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `(МГУ, 2012)` | unchanged |
| `Образование (МГУ)` | unchanged |
| `в МГТУ им. Баумана` | unchanged |
| `Обучение: Skillbox, 2020` | unchanged |

## Lower priority: over-redaction from the new company cues

This is the safe direction, but it costs readability, and these are technologies, not companies:

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `опыт в Python и Go` | `опыт в [REDACTED] и [REDACTED]` |
| `опыт в SQL, Excel и Power BI` | `опыт в [REDACTED], [REDACTED] и [REDACTED]` |
| `Kubernetes (5 лет)` | `[REDACTED] (5 лет)` |
| `Python (2 года), Go (3 года)` | `[REDACTED] (2 года), [REDACTED] (3 года)` |
| `проекты для Telegram` | `проекты для [REDACTED]` |
| `Роль в Scrum: мастер` | `Роль в [REDACTED]: мастер` |

## Lower priority: cost

`organization-experience` and the cues add time on long lines: on one laptop, a 9 KB JSON line went from about 34 ms on 0.16.2 to about 72 ms on 0.17.0, on the main thread of a synchronous caller. A 267-byte line went from about 3.3 ms to 3.9 ms.

## Must stay unchanged

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Опыт: 3 года, 5 месяцев` | unchanged |
| `Директор, руководитель отдела` | unchanged |
| `Встреча, понедельник (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Отпуск (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `order 89161234567 shipped` | unchanged |
| `id 79161234567` | unchanged |
| `Встреча в понедельник с Романом` | unchanged |
| `Использовал Kubernetes и PostgreSQL` | unchanged |

## Expected

1. A date range anchors an entry whatever word its title starts with, and whatever comes before the entry on the line. The employer is replaced in sections 1 to 3.
2. A Russian mobile number after a comma is replaced in document prose, without touching the `order` and `id` controls.
3. The school rows are replaced, or `docs/COVERAGE.md` lists them as limits.
4. Well-known technology names under the new cues stay, or the over-redaction is documented.

## Acceptance

- Every row in sections 1 to 3 and the phone section is replaced, in text and JSON mode.
- The "Must stay unchanged" rows stay unchanged.
- Tests use several titles outside the current list, not only the ones above, so the fix doesn't grow the list by these words alone.

title: build(deps): refresh dependencies and repair upgrade regressions
body:
Fixes #102

The merged Dependabot updates exposed stale workflow assertions, formatter changes and incomplete local-package lock metadata. This PR repairs those failures while preserving the upgrades, then refreshes the full npm, Deno, Python, Actions, toolchain and container dependency trees.

- Regenerate all three npm locks and the frozen Deno graph; add a complete hash-locked Python benchmark graph. Synchronize active version pins and retain the patch Changeset for automated release.
- Use current Node 26.13.0/npm 12.2.2, Bun 1.4.4, Deno 2.9.8 and exact current Action releases. Install npm before setup-node cache discovery. Lock the preview browser tools and match their Playwright container digest.
- Replace handwritten semantic-version comparison and Windows command wrappers with `semver` and `cmd-shim`. Delegate BuildKit pull retries to the current upstream Action while preserving registry fallback, opt-out and tracing.
- Derive benchmark scanner expectations from requirements, and exercise the actual hash-verified spaCy model and offline scanners in security CI. Keep artifact authentication/digests, extraction compatibility, cleanup callbacks and release behavior.

The [implementation comparison](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/compare/15f86c08069a53c65020fdb760512aac37929976...f52f39156884a6d10882e28c9b898a1b21b417a3) contains the 63 code/configuration changes before the raw evidence publication. The final publication also clarifies the contributor documentation.

### Dependency evidence and compatibility limits

[Evidence index](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-102-b6ecf86c9f05/dev/log/issues/102/pulls/103/README.md), [requirement mapping](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-102-b6ecf86c9f05/dev/log/issues/102/pulls/103/PLAN.md), [root-cause/migration analysis](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-102-b6ecf86c9f05/dev/log/issues/102/pulls/103/ANALYSIS.md) and [complete dependency tables](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/tree/issue-102-b6ecf86c9f05/dev/log/issues/102/pulls/103/dependencies) record every old/latest/resolved entry, source and retained constraint. These include transitive packages, removed/hoisted entries, inline tools, images and all 67 external Action references.

Python 3.14.10 is the latest compatible security release: current Presidio caps preshed below the release that fixes Python 3.15 model loading. An actual CI reproduction fails with `OverflowError`; the same scanner test passes on 3.14.10. Temurin 21.0.13+9 remains the latest supported Java 21 patch for Capacitor's current Gradle template; Java 27 requires an unsupported template/toolchain migration. Other retained transitive versions name their upstream consumer constraints individually. All audited dependency graphs have zero reported vulnerabilities.

### Reproduction and verification

On baseline main `15f86c0`, the Checks workflow fails Prettier at three loop statements, Workflows rejects its upgraded zizmor pair, and Example app installation rejects missing local rimraf metadata. Preserved complete logs and exact error lines are linked from [VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-102-b6ecf86c9f05/dev/log/issues/102/pulls/103/VALIDATION.md).

Regression coverage includes `tests/ci-workflow-policy.test.js`, `tests/workflows-lint.test.js`, `tests/pipeline-requirements.test.js`, `tests/temp-cleanup.test.js`, `tests/changeset-config.test.js`, `tests/node-toolchain.test.js`, `tests/setup-npm.test.js` and the Python version/audit tests. CI also runs the real upstream Buildx Action/daemon with bounded recovered/exhausted pull faults and the actual NLP scanner smoke. No failing tests were skipped.

Local focused regressions, ESLint, Prettier, Ruff, actionlint, ShellCheck, zizmor, Vite production build, artifact archive roundtrip and desktop compatibility probes pass. The archive/desktop probes make deprecations fatal. All three npm audits, the complete 69-package Python audit and development-tool audit report zero findings. Full Node/Bun/Deno and Linux/Windows/macOS coverage runs on existing CI to respect the local memory limit; [live PR checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/pull/103/checks) identify the current commit. Optional Android/iOS dispatch jobs retain their existing opt-in policy and are not represented as successful PR builds.

### Upstream reports

Existing upstream discussions were searched before reporting; exact report bodies and returned URLs are saved under the evidence folder.

| Dependency / retained integration | Report |
| --- | --- |
| temp legacy cleanup | [node-temp 100](https://github.com/bruce/node-temp/issues/100#issuecomment-6672682111) |
| Artifact unzip Buffer deprecation | [toolkit 2003](https://github.com/actions/toolkit/issues/2003#issuecomment-6672682500) |
| actionlint job self-reference | [actionlint 711](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/issues/711#issuecomment-6672682896) |
| actionlint concurrency queue schema | [actionlint 657](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/issues/657#issuecomment-6672683280) |
| setup-node/npm cache ordering | [setup-node 1553](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1553#issuecomment-6672683784) |
| PyYAML Python 3.15 wheel availability | [PyYAML 951](https://github.com/yaml/pyyaml/issues/951#issuecomment-6672684219) |
| Buildx registry failover | [setup-buildx 490](https://github.com/docker/setup-buildx-action/pull/490#issuecomment-6672972223) |
| Artifact finalization retry/reconciliation | [upload-artifact 531](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/issues/531#issuecomment-6672972696) |
| archiver-utils glob range | [node-archiver 822](https://github.com/archiverjs/node-archiver/issues/822#issuecomment-6672973126) |
| Pages creation retry/reconciliation | [deploy-pages 454](https://github.com/actions/deploy-pages/issues/454) |
| Presidio's cap excludes the Python 3.15 fix | [Presidio 2431](https://github.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/issues/2431#issuecomment-6673100519) |

The latest main is included. The issue's literal requirement for a new green run on main remains pending the normal PR merge and its CI run; this PR does not merge or write directly to main.

title: feat: close document sanitization gaps and add sensitive fields
body:
Fix document sanitization gaps in URL queries, CVs, structured fields and escaped records. Add synchronous `sensitiveFields` declarations so callers can redact complete JSON/JSONL property values without a new recognizer release.

## Changes

- Protect plain/percent-encoded email and phone queries in absolute/relative URLs and access logs, personal paths under arbitrary labels, and opaque share links.
- Cover complex dated CV entries, multi-word employer labels, company cues/lists/durations, split signatures, school verbs and role labels.
- Normalize the documented structured field vocabulary across camelCase/snake_case/kebab-case; add exact caller-declared sensitive properties for strings, primitives and containers in both synchronous and asynchronous APIs.
- Preserve empty children attributes and subsequent lines; replace no-progress escaped fragments while retaining parseable records.
- Document ambiguous undated employers/personal website roots and synchronous customization using existing `knownPersonal` lists or exact-input `findings`. `detectors` remains asynchronous-only.
- Include one minor Changeset for the next automated release.

## Requirements and research

[Complete requirement-by-requirement analysis, alternatives, source links and reported-row inventory](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-100-3ee178fbdee1/docs/case-studies/issue-100/README.md).

Researched the WHATWG URL Standard, existing libphonenumber-js matching, Presidio recognizers and Google Drive sharing semantics. Reused native scanners and source-offset mapping; no new dependencies or model downloads.

The requirement to publish #90 is already resolved: the reporter confirms npm 0.16.2, verified against npm metadata and GitHub release v0.16.2 (published November 5, 2026). This PR prepares the subsequent release through Changesets.

## Reproduction and verification

Use `sanitize(input, { profile: 'documents' })`, or sanitize `JSON.stringify({note: input})` with `structured: 'json'`. Examples that previously leaked: `Компания: Ромашка Лютик`, `https://example.org/p?email=anna.smirnova%40example.org`, and the dated CV rows recorded in the inventory. `experiments/issue-100/` contains bounded reproductions, including the doubly escaped fragment.

- The original code fails 65 of the first 80 regression cases; fixed code passes all 84, including overlapping-credential schema, punctuation and comma-spacing regressions.
- The initial focused document/experience/escape suites passed together (495 tests). After CI exposed a punctuation regression, the corrected document/CV/reversible-placeholder suites passed all 130 tests.
- ESLint passes with zero warnings; changed files are formatted.
- All four workflows passed for final commit `8b1d9d3`: [Checks and release](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42102524772), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42102524797), [Example app](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42102525055), and [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42102524955). The full Linux Node suite reports 2,939 passed, zero failed and one skipped; all Node/Bun/Deno runtime shards across Linux/macOS/Windows passed. GitHub reports 52 successful checks and ten intentionally skipped release/deployment/mobile jobs. The initial Node/Deno logs identified a sentence-ending period consumed by a company token (run 42101831141, Node log line 3867); bounded company tokens and separate list entities now preserve punctuation and placeholder identity.

Permitted coverage limits are explicitly documented and tested: the three undated employer fragments and personal website root. All dated CV rows and mandatory contextual company rows are implemented. Existing preservation controls remain unchanged.

Fixes #100
Fixes #91
Fixes #94

Final review: the branch contains current `main`; the working tree is clean; all implementation commits are pushed; no previous features were intentionally removed.

Updates `jscpd` from 5.4.0 to 5.4.2
Release notes

Sourced from jscpd's releases.

Release v5.4.2

The post What's new in jscpd 5.4.2 shows the new features with commands and real output.

New Features

  • Boundaries keep the code of a module inside it. The new boundaries key of the config file lists rules. A rule names the code it protects (code: a folder, a file, a glob, or a method as path#name), where copies of it must not show up (notIn, or every file outside code when it is left out) and where they may after all (allow). Every clone run checks the rules, and a copy of protected code outside its boundary fails the run with exit code 1. Import linters miss such copies, because a copied function imports nothing.

    • jscpd looks for copies three ways, and a rule can set its own bars in thresholds. Token clones find copy-paste, the structure comparison of --similarity finds an edited copy, and the --semantic model finds the same logic written again, often in another language. disable turns kinds off by their --kind names. Without a downloaded model, jscpd prints a warning and checks the rules without the semantic search.
    • A mistake in a rule, such as an unknown key or a glob that doesn't compile, stops the run with an error that names the rule. A rule that checks nothing in a run, after a typo in a path or a method name for example, gets a warning.
    • The console, console-full, ai and json reporters show the violations, the json one under boundaries. Baselines and --changed don't apply to violations yet, and SARIF, the language server and the MCP server don't report them.
    • fixtures/boundaries-demo is a small shop whose web app copies the backend's pricing and loan code. (#1225, #1227)

  • --ignore-identifiers pairs a name with one name. Every name used to match every other name, so x = x + x * x was a clone of d = a + b * c, although its data flows another way. Now a name on one side has to stand for the same name on the other side every time, and two names can't stand for one, as in Baker's parameterized matching and NiCad's consistent renaming. On 24 projects in 11 languages, 6,942 of the 14,501 renamed clones that the old matching reported had no such mapping.

    • jscpd cuts a clone where a name starts to stand for two and still reports every part of --min-tokens tokens or more.
    • A name reached as a member, after . or ?., and after -> in C, C++, PHP and Perl, is another name than a local of the same text. A constructor that sets this.url = url still matches its copy that sets this.url = link (#1220).
    • --ignore-identifiers and --ignore-identifiers=consistent give the new matching, --ignore-identifiers=blind the old one. The config takes "ignoreIdentifiers": true, "consistent" or "blind", and the Action input takes consistent or blind. The value goes after = only, so --ignore-identifiers src/ still scans src/.
    • fixtures/type2-demo has the consistent and members examples. (#1217, #1218)

  • --similarity pairs a name with one name too. The fingerprint of a subtree now records how its names repeat, so x = x + x * x no longer scores 1.0 against d = a + b * c, and a renamed copy still does. Members, labels such as keyword arguments and object keys, and types each have names of their own, so self.url = url still matches self.url = link. A function's own name matches any name. Kotlin's true, false and null and Clojure's true, false and nil are literals now. On the same 24 projects, 15 of 23,530 pairs fell below 0.8, and runs take 2 to 9% longer. --ignore-identifiers=blind brings back the old scores and also turns on renamed token clones. fixtures/similarity-demo/names scores a renamed copy at 1.00 and a mirrored function at 0.74. (#1219)

  • --history tracks the health score, and a bare --history walks the last 30 commits. Every commit of the series gets the score that jscpd --health gives its tree. The console draws a health chart under the duplication chart and adds HEALTH and CHANGE columns, and every point of the JSON report has health. --health and --dashboard take --history now: the badge or the dashboard comes first, then the series, in the markdown and html reports too.

    • jscpd --history used to fail with "a value is required". Without a value the flag takes the config's history, or else the newest 30 commits of HEAD (--history-limit). --history-every N spaces them N commits apart, and the Action's history input takes true.
    • jscpd scans a commit the way it scans the working tree: --ignore and --pattern see its files at their working-tree paths, and the checkout runs none of the repository's hooks. A walk that stops at the edge of a shallow clone prints a warning that names the commit.
    • The last 30 commits of axios take about 5.4 seconds, against 4.9 without the health score. (#1199)

  • jscpd knows 73 more formats by extension, and files by name. 94 of 224 formats had no built-in extension, a gap that came from v4, so jscpd . skipped Dockerfiles, Makefiles, go.mod, Elixir and Nix files unless you mapped them. The new extensions come from GitHub Linguist, and a table of file names maps Dockerfile, Containerfile, Makefile, go.mod, CMakeLists.txt, Gemfile, Jenkinsfile and others. Existing formats got more suffixes, such as .zsh, .jsonc, .tfvars and .sbt. A Markdown fence such as ```dockerfile takes its format from the same table, and --formats-exts and --formats-names still win over every built-in mapping. FORMATS.md lists the file names too. (#1174, #1192)

Changes

  • jscpd . scans more files. On 22 repositories the new file associations picked up 1 to 5 more files each, mostly Dockerfiles, .editorconfig, .jsonc, Makefiles and go.mod, and jscpd scans the .rst files of Sphinx docs like Markdown. The duplication percentage can move, and a --threshold gate can fail. (#1192)

  • --ignore-identifiers reports fewer renamed clones, and some of them are shorter. A baseline that 5.4 made with --ignore-identifiers is a blind one. Keep --ignore-identifiers=blind with it or update the baseline, or --fail-on-new-clones reports the cut clones as new. (#1218)

  • --history walks first parents. A merged branch counts as its merge commit, so a range across merged branches gives fewer points than before. jscpd builds a series only when a reporter shows it (console, console-full, ai or json, and markdown or html with --health or --dashboard), so a badge-only --health job no longer walks the range. The ai lines read 37be780 2026-08-08 2/1/47.6 +47.6 health 72 -2 now, and a wrong health or dead-code option no longer fails a clone run. (#1199)

Bug Fixes

  • jscpd aborted on a Markdown page whose front matter ran into a code fence. A page that opens with a horizontal rule and later shows a Python stub had front matter from the rule down to the stub's ..., across the fence, and the scan panicked: jscpd exited with 134, and jscpd --mcp and jscpd --lsp died. A --- on the first line now opens front matter only when the next line isn't blank, as Pandoc reads it, and only a --- or ... line before the first code fence closes it. The frontmatter of an Astro component follows the same rule. A page of code fences that never close used to take quadratic time, 3.9 seconds for 100 KB, and takes 0.04 seconds now. (#1223, #1226)

  • A Razor view was read out of order. jscpd tokenized the HTML of a whole view and then the C# of its blocks, so a clone across that seam ended before it started: release builds printed ranges such as [48:48 - 5:35], and debug builds panicked. A view is now one stream in the order of its text. Two identical views count as duplicated from the first line to the last, and markup in an @if or @foreach block matches the same markup outside one. (#1221, #1222)

  • The MCP server's check_duplication never matched a Vue, Svelte or Astro snippet. It tokenized a snippet as one stream, while a scan splits a component into its blocks and a Markdown file into its prose and fences. A component snippet met only the components inside Markdown fences, by meaning it found nothing, and the fences of a Markdown snippet matched nothing either. The server now splits a snippet the way a scan splits a file of its format. Each match has format and lines, and the note names every block too short to match. #1228 also fixed how jscpd counts the duplicated lines of a clone whose two fragments swap places, so the statistics of a --cross-formats run can change a little. (#1224, #1228, #1229)

  • --history failed when git's log.showSignature was on. git printed the signature check of each signed commit before the commit, and jscpd took that line for a commit hash. jscpd now passes --no-show-signature and reads only lines that start with a commit hash. Reported with an exact reproduction by @​vitorcsbrito. (#1195, #1196)

  • --compare paired a function with every near-best lookalike. It took the rule of --semantic, where a group of near-equal functions all pair with each other, but in a port a function has one counterpart. A pair now stays only when it is the best match of one of its two functions, and a near tie goes to the partner in a file of the same name. On the analysis modules of Lucene and Lucene.NET the pairs went from 2,219 to 1,392, and the share of pairs between files of the same name from 46% to 73%. Analysis and numbers by @​MysterionRise. (#1162, #1194)

  • --semantic reported a page and the component it renders as a clone. It skips a pair when one function calls the other, but it didn't count a JSX element such as <EditUserForm /> as a call. It does now, and so does the call graph of --compare. Reported by @​Rosenblad, fixed by @​cristianchiriac. (#1210, #1211)

  • Reports named a clone in a Markdown block or a component like guide.md:markup. The VS Code extension opened that name as a file and failed. The JSON name, the language server's jscpd/clones and jscpd/semantic, the XML path and the xcode location now name the file, and the JSON keeps the block's language in format. The console, ai and HTML reports still name the block. (#1200)

How to prepare a release

  3. Update the version in https://github.com/actions/cache/blob/main/package.json.

  7. Run licensed status and resolve any warnings by updating the https://github.com/actions/cache/blob/main/.licensed.yml file with the exceptions.
  8. Commit your changes and push your branch upstream.
  9. Open a pull request against main and get it reviewed and merged.
  10. Draft a new release https://github.com/actions/cache/releases use the same version number used in package.json
    1. Create a new tag with the version number.
    2. Auto generate release notes and update them to match the changes you made in RELEASES.md.

title: Fix preview container tooling and complete Python CI coverage
body:
The main screenshot writer failed with `gh: command not found` in the pinned Playwright container ([failing run](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42080626844)). Install the official GitHub CLI with a pinned checksum and run a real, read-only credential-helper smoke check in the same container on PRs before the main writer. Both event filters now cover the writer's helper dependencies.

The complete JavaScript/Python template comparison also identified missing Python coverage. Add pinned Ruff checks and precommit formatting, Python CodeQL, Python file-size enforcement, and a metadata-only transitive requirements audit using uv/pip-audit. Add grouped weekly Dependabot updates for every actual manifest. Keep six measured expensive test suites distributed as files are added, expand macOS Deno to six shards to eliminate the observed budget warnings without increasing timeouts, and update status-gate count assertions for the new jobs. Separate cold subprocess startup from the unchanged two-second scanner assertions in PuTTY/whitespace regression probes, reusing the established process-tree hang guard. Existing release, runtime, artifact, Pages and scanner behavior is preserved; a patch changeset prepares the next release.

### Investigation and reproduction

- [Analysis, timeline, complete requirement mapping and options](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-95-5445009fe5d0/dev/log/issues/95/pulls/96/ANALYSIS.md)
- [Template comparison and all 17 best-practice decisions](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-95-5445009fe5d0/dev/log/issues/95/pulls/96/TEMPLATE-REVIEW.md), [individual CI path dispositions](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-95-5445009fe5d0/dev/log/issues/95/pulls/96/TEMPLATE-PATHS.md), and complete source archives/tree inventories in the evidence directory.
- All seven cited runs, job metadata, annotations, full compressed logs and the original screenshot artifact are preserved under `dev/log/issues/95/pulls/96/`. The green-log error-like strings are passing test fixtures or echoed options; the historical Ubuntu migration notice and documented OpenSSL combined-bundle handling belong to GitHub's generated graph workflow. A broader warning/deprecation scan is also preserved and classified.
- `python3 experiments/issue-95/verify-regression.py` substitutes the issue baseline workflows/size script and restores them after demonstrating seven failing regression checks. The isolated-PATH test reproduces the missing CLI without credentials. `verify-preview-tools.py` verifies the real downloaded CLI and credential helper.
- Shared template defect reported with a container reproduction, workaround and code suggestions: https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/285.

### Validation

- 90 focused Node tests, the additional dependency-update scope test, 13 initial shard/status integration tests, the final 47-test shard/budget/workflow suite, 15 scanner/startup regression tests under Node and Bun, and five small Python audit unit tests passed locally.
- Real checksum-verified CLI installation/credential smoke and a 69-package hashed Python dependency audit passed, without installing NLP packages or models.
- Workflow policy, terminal-gate coverage, Ruff, ESLint/Prettier and shell precommit checks passed. New failure fixtures capture expected annotations so they cannot generate false CI errors.
