title: knownPersonal matches inside words: 'Lee' in 'Sleep' → 'S[PERSON_1]p', 'Смирнов' → '[PERSON_1]ка'
body:
## Problem

`knownPersonal` values match **inside** longer words, case-insensitively, with no word boundary. Placeholder output then cuts words apart.

v0.13.0 (ee7b51c), `sanitize(text, { knownPersonal: [{ type: 'PERSON', value }], transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', format: '[{TYPE}_{n}]', map: false } })`:

| known value | text | known-personal findings | output |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Павлов` | `Отчество: Сергей Павлович.` | `Павлов` | `Отчество: [PERSON_1].` |
| `Арсенова` | `Автор: Сарсенова Анна.` | `арсенова` | `Автор: [PERSON_1].` |
| `Смирнов` | `Город: Смирновка.` | `Смирнов` | `Город: [PERSON_1]ка.` |
| `Lee` | `Sleep well, Lee.` | `lee`, `Lee` | `S[PERSON_1]p well, [PERSON_1].` |
| `Ann` | `Annual report by Ann.` | `Ann`, `Ann` | `[PERSON_1]ual report by [PERSON_1].` |

- `Lee` inside `Sleep` and `Ann` inside `Annual` show that any short known name corrupts ordinary words.
- `Арсенова` inside `Сарсенова` (a different surname) matches mid-word, lowercase.
- `Смирнов` → `[PERSON_1]ка` and `Павлов` inside the patronymic `Павлович` show a prefix match that cuts the word.

This also makes known-value scans noisy: a verification pass reports "known value still present" for text that holds only other words.

## Expected

- A known value matches only at word boundaries (Unicode letters and digits on both sides count as word characters), so `Lee` does not match in `Sleep` and `Арсенова` does not match in `Сарсенова`.
- When a known value is found as a prefix of a longer word, the whole word is replaced, never `[PERSON_1]ка`. Inflected forms are a separate request (#60), and they should be matched as whole words too.
- Case-insensitive matching is fine, but not across a lowercase→uppercase word start (`арсенова` in `Сарсенова`).

title: Replace only knownPersonal values with a restore map (known scores 0.85 < detections 0.9; redact() returns no map)
body:
## Problem

There is no way to replace **only** the caller's known values while keeping a restore map.

Use case: a document contains a few real people (known list) and also deliberately fictional example names, sample phones and company names that must stay as they are. The goal is to replace exactly the known values, reversibly.

v0.13.0 (ee7b51c), text:

```
Отчёт подготовил Петров Данил Сергеевич. Пример в документации: Иванов Иван Иванович, тел. +7 900 000-00-00, ООО «Ромашка», г. Казань.
```

`knownPersonal: [{ type: 'PERSON', value: 'Петров Данил Сергеевич' }]`, `profile: 'documents'`:

`inspect()` findings:

```
PERSON 0.85 "Петров Данил Сергеевич" known-personal
PERSON 0.9  "Петров Данил Сергеевич" name-identity
PERSON 0.9  "Иванов Иван Иванович"   name-identity
PERSON 0.7  "Иван Иванович"          name-gazetteer
PHONE  0.85 "+7 900 000-00-00"       international-phone
ORGANIZATION 0.7 "ООО «Ромашка»"     organization-legal-form
LOCATION 0.75 "Казань."              location-label
```

What the existing options give:

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| `minConfidence: 0.85` | `[PERSON_1] … [PERSON_2], тел. [PHONE_1]` (example name and phone replaced) |
| `minConfidence: 0.9` | `[PERSON_1] … [PERSON_2]` (example name replaced) |
| `minConfidence: 1` | nothing replaced, known value included |
| `inspect()` → keep `rule === 'known-personal'` → `redact(text, findings, { transformation: { mode: 'placeholder' } })` | `Отчёт подготовил [PERSON_1]. … Иванов Иван Иванович …` as a plain **string**: correct text, but **no restore map** |

So known values score below ordinary detections (0.85 vs 0.9), and the one path that isolates them (`redact`) drops the map.

## Expected

Any of:

1. An option such as `detection: 'known'` / `knownOnly: true` for `sanitize()` that turns off automatic personal detection and replaces only `knownPersonal` (and `knownSecrets`) values; credentials could still be protected unless `credentialsOnly`-style filtering is asked for.
2. `redact()` with `transformation: { mode: 'placeholder' }` returning `{ text, map }` like `sanitize()`, so callers can supply their own findings and still restore.
3. Known values scored at confidence 1.0, so `minConfidence: 1` keeps only them (simplest, but mixes two meanings into one threshold).

The same applies to `mode: 'fake'`: a known-only run should not rewrite fictional example names.

title: fake mode: Russian given names (Данил, Максим, Алина) become surnames, and one given name can stay unchanged
body:
## Problem

In `transformation: { mode: 'fake' }`, Russian names are rewritten part by part, but several common given names are classified as surnames. The fake then has two surnames, which reads as a broken name and changes the name's shape:

Input: `Автор: <name>.`, key `example-key-0123456789abcdef`, v0.13.0 (ee7b51c).

| Input | fake, detection only | fake, with `knownPersonal: [{type:'PERSON', value:<name>}]` |
|---|---|---|
| Петров Данил Сергеевич | Баранов Муравьев Филимонович | Баранов Муравьев Филимонович |
| Данил Сергеевич Петров | Данил Филимонович Баранов | Муравьев Филимонович Баранов |
| Петров Данил | Баранов Муравьев | Баранов Муравьев |
| Данил Петров | Муравьев Баранов | Муравьев Баранов |
| Кузнецов Максим Антонович | Колесников Рожков Гавриилович | Колесников Рожков Гавриилович |
| Максим Кузнецов | Рожков Колесников | Рожков Колесников |
| Смирнова Алина | Потапова Мамонтова | Потапова Мамонтова |
| Алина Смирнова | Мамонтова Потапова | Мамонтова Потапова |
| Соколова Мария Ивановна | Данилова Элеонора Харитоновна | Данилова Элеонора Харитоновна |

Observations:

1. `Данил`, `Максим`, `Алина` get surname fakes in every word order; `Мария` is handled correctly. The patronymic is enough context to know the middle token is a given name, but it is still faked as a surname.
2. Row 2, detection only: the given name `Данил` is left **unchanged** while the rest is faked, so part of the real name stays in the output. With `knownPersonal` it is replaced (but as a surname).
3. Gender agreement of surname and patronymic is right; only the role of the given-name token is wrong.

## Expected

- In `Surname Given [Patronymic]` and `Given [Patronymic] Surname` forms, the given-name slot gets a given-name fake of the same gender (`Петров Данил Сергеевич` → e.g. `Баранов Игорь Филимонович`).
- A token inside a detected person span is never left as is (row 2).
- When the role of a token is unknown, the whole span is replaced with a complete fake name of the same shape instead of a per-token guess.

A deterministic way to decide the slot: a token followed by a patronymic (`-ович/-евич/-ична/-овна/-евна`) is a given name; with two tokens, the one that matches surname morphology (`-ов/-ев/-ин/-ский/-ова/-ева/-ина/-ская`) is the surname. A larger given-name list would also fix these specific names.

## Use case

Replacing real names in test fixtures and example data with consistent, natural-looking fakes so the text keeps reading like the original (one surname, one given name, gender kept).

title: Context credential rule redacts prose: 'signal is …', 'pass is …', 'file.ts:365) | …'
knownPersonal and map entries: match inflected and partial forms of the same entity
body:
## Problem

`knownPersonal` is the best tool when the caller already knows the private values (for example from the structured fields of the same record). With it, every exact mention is replaced. But in Russian (and other inflected languages) the same entity mostly appears in other case forms, and those stay in the output:

```js
const knownPersonal = [
  { type: 'LOCATION', value: 'Кострома' },
  { type: 'ORGANIZATION', value: 'Ромашка' },
  { type: 'PERSON', value: 'Анна Смирнова' },
];
const opts = { profile: 'documents', knownPersonal,
  transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', map: createRestoreMap({ format: '[{TYPE}_{n}]' }) } };

sanitize('Кострома; ООО «Ромашка»', opts).text;              // "[LOCATION_1]; [ORGANIZATION_1]"  ok
sanitize('Живу в Костроме, работал в Ромашке.', opts).text;  // unchanged
sanitize('Отзыв от Анны Смирновой', opts).text;              // unchanged
sanitize('Смирновой Анне', opts).text;                       // unchanged
```

Person linking already handles masculine `-ов/-ев` surnames (`Ивановым`), but not feminine `-ова/-ева` (`Смирновой`), given names (`Анны`, `Анне`), or the case forms of organizations and places (`Костроме`, `Ромашке`). In model-written summaries about a document, inflected mentions are the norm, so a sanitized summary still names the person, the employer and the city.

A related gap: a known multi-word organization (`ООО «Северная торговая компания»`) is often mentioned later by its distinctive part only (`Северная торговая компания`, `в Северной торговой компании`).

## Proposal

- For `knownPersonal` and for entities already in the restore map, also match bounded inflected forms per locale. For Russian: noun/adjective case endings for the last letters of each word (`-а/-ы/-е/-у/-ой/-ою`, `-ий/-ого/-ому/-им/-ом`, `-ь/-я/-ю/-ем/-и`, feminine surnames `-ова/-ой`, `-ая/-ой/-ую`), with a minimum stem length so short words do not over-match.
- Match the distinctive part of a known organization (without the legal form and quotes), including its inflected forms.
- Each matched surface is stored as a separate original surface of the same entry, so exact restore keeps working, as it already does for `Ивановым`.
- Optional, for structured input: `personalFields: { 'company': 'ORGANIZATION', 'first_name': 'PERSON', … }` to take known values from fields of the same JSON record and apply them to all its other strings, so callers do not have to collect them manually.

## Acceptance

- All four examples above produce placeholders for every mention, and `restore` returns the exact input.
- No new replacements on existing fixtures that do not use `knownPersonal`.

title: documents profile: Russian employer, school and city forms that are still missed
body:
## Problem

The `documents` profile (thanks for #55) catches `ООО Ромашка`, `ООО "Север Плюс"` and `ООО ТЕХНОСОФТ`. On Russian CVs, though, most employers, schools and cities still come through. Measured on a corpus of Russian-language CVs against their own structured fields (employer/school/city lists), detection alone missed about 68% of employer mentions, 16 of 17 school mentions and about half of the city mentions. Synthetic reproductions with `profile: 'documents'` and placeholder mode:

| Input | Output today | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `ООО «Северная торговая компания» — менеджер` | unchanged | `[ORGANIZATION_1] — менеджер` (lowercase words inside the quoted name) |
| `АО «Гранит-2» — инженер` | unchanged | digits and hyphens inside the quoted name |
| `Работал в ООО «Ромашка» и затем в Ромашка.` | `[ORGANIZATION_1] … в Ромашка.` | the bare name of an already detected organization is the same entity |
| `Ромашка Групп, ведущий инженер` | unchanged | `Групп`/`Group`/`Холдинг`/`Holding` as organization markers |
| `Московский государственный университет, 2015` | unchanged | adjective + lowercase words + institution type word |
| `Северный федеральный университет имени Ломоносова` | unchanged | `имени <Name>` tail is part of the name |
| `Санкт-Петербургский политехнический университет` | unchanged | hyphenated adjectival city prefix |
| `НИУ ВШЭ, магистратура` | unchanged | institution acronyms after type acronyms (`НИУ`, `МГУ`-style uppercase acronyms in an education context) |
| `Город: Кострома` | unchanged | location label followed by a colon |
| `Проживаю: Кострома` / `Кострома, готов к переезду` | unchanged | common residence phrasing |
| `Ярославль, Россия` | unchanged | `<City>, <Country>` pattern; also a larger city list (a regional city of ~600k people is missing) |
| `Меня зовут Анна, я тестировщик.` / `С уважением, Анна` | unchanged | a single given name after a self-introduction or a sign-off (`С уважением, Анна Смирнова` already works) |

## Proposal

- In quoted names after a legal form, accept the whole quoted span (any words, digits, hyphens, up to a bound) instead of capitalized words only.
- Propagate a detected organization's core name (the quoted part / the part without the legal form) to its other mentions in the same document or stream.
- Russian education names: an optional adjectival prefix (`…ский`, `…ный`, `…вый`, hyphenated forms), lowercase words up to the institution type word, an optional `имени …` tail; uppercase acronyms in an education context.
- Location labels with `:` and residence phrases; a `<City>, <Country>` pattern; a larger bounded offline vocabulary, e.g. GeoNames `cities15000` subset per locale (already mentioned in the #56 case study).
- Given name alone after self-introduction / sign-off phrases, using the existing name gazetteer.

All of this can stay inside the opt-in `documents` profile with lower confidence, as now.

## Acceptance

Each row above produces the expected output under `profile: 'documents'`, with fixtures, and the existing default-profile fixtures do not change.

title: Placeholder mode refuses ordinary text containing GPT-4, ISO-9001, Windows-10 (ERR_PLACEHOLDER_COLLISION)
body:
## Problem

With the default placeholder format `{Type}-{n}`, `sanitize` throws `ERR_PLACEHOLDER_COLLISION` for any text containing an ordinary `Letters-Number` token, even when that token has nothing to do with the placeholder labels:

```js
import { sanitize, createRestoreMap } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const t = { transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', map: createRestoreMap() } };
sanitize('Jane Doe knows GPT-4.', t);          // throws ERR_PLACEHOLDER_COLLISION
sanitize('Jane Doe, ISO-9001 audits', t);      // throws
sanitize('Jane Doe uses Windows-10', t);       // throws
sanitize('Jane Doe uses Python 3', t);         // ok -> "Person-1 uses Python 3"
```

The namespace check in `src/placeholders.js` (`preparePlaceholderText`) turns `{Type}` into `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*` and `{n}` into `[1-9][0-9]*`, without word boundaries. So `GPT-4`, `ISO-9001`, `COVID-19`, `Web-3`, `SQL-92`, `S-300` and even `abc-1` inside a longer word all count as collisions.

On a corpus of technical CVs (version numbers, standards, product names), every single document was refused with the default format. Switching to `[{TYPE}_{n}]` avoided it, but the default should work on normal prose.

## Expected

- Reserve only labels the sanitizer can actually emit (`Person`, `Organization`, `Education`, `Location`, `Email`, `Phone`, `Date`, `Credential` and the other detector type labels, in the casing the template uses), not every identifier.
- Match with token boundaries, so `xPerson-1y` and `Person-1a` are not collisions, while a standalone `Person-1` still is.
- When a map is reused, an existing token of that map in the input is still a collision (as today).

## Acceptance

- The four examples above succeed with the default format; `GPT-4`, `ISO-9001` and `Windows-10` stay unchanged in the output and restore exactly.
- `sanitize('Person-1 met Jane Doe', ...)` still throws `ERR_PLACEHOLDER_COLLISION`.

title: feat: Add reversible placeholders and multilingual document entities
body:

title: Detect organizations, schools and locations without a preceding context word
body:
## Problem

Organizations are only detected after a context word. The rule in `src/personal.js` matches a capitalized word directly after `компании|организации|company|organization|société|empresa|Firma`. Typical documents name employers, schools and places without such a word, so they stay in the output:

```
2019–2023  Acme Ltd, Senior Engineer
2015–2019  Northfield State University
Based in Springfield, relocated from Riverton
```

None of `Acme Ltd`, `Northfield State University`, `Springfield` or `Riverton` is a finding today, as far as I can tell from the rules. The same holds for other languages, e.g. `ООО «Ромашка»`, `Ромашка GmbH`.

Together with names, these quasi-identifiers (employer + school + city + years) are often enough to re-identify a person. That makes "the output is anonymous" claims weak for CVs, profiles and similar documents even when every name and email is removed.

## Proposal

- **Organizations by legal form**, with or without quotes and in either order, e.g. `Inc`, `LLC`, `Ltd`, `GmbH`, `AG`, `S.A.`, `ООО`, `АО`, `ПАО`, `ИП`, plus the other locales of the gazetteer.
- **Educational institutions** by type words (`University`, `College`, `Institute`, `Университет`, `Институт`…) next to a proper name.
- **Locations** (cities, regions) from a bounded gazetteer and after location labels (`based in`, `located in`, `г.`, `город`).
- **New types**, so placeholder/fake modes can number them: `ORGANIZATION`, `EDUCATION` (or `ORGANIZATION` with a subtype) and `LOCATION`.
- **Public exemptions** keep working through the existing `publicEntities` list, for organizations that are fine to keep, and through `knownPersonal` for ones that must always go.
- **Confidence.** These findings are lower-confidence than identifiers. Expose a confidence and a profile switch, so log sanitization does not suddenly redact every capitalized company name in stack traces.

## Acceptance

- Fixtures for each supported locale with employers, schools and cities in list form (no context words) are detected.
- No new findings on the existing credential/log fixtures under the default profile.
- `COVERAGE.md` lists the new types and their limits.

title: Reversible typed placeholders (Person-1, Organization-1) with a private restore map (JSON / Links Notation) and a no-map full anonymization mode
body:
## Problem

None of the current transformations gives readable, consistent placeholders that can be reversed by the data owner:

| Mode | Output for `Jane Doe` | Same person twice → same token | Readable | Reversible |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `redact` | `[REDACTED]` | no (every person is the same token) | yes | no |
| `pseudonym` | `[PSEUDONYM_3f9a…]` (24 hex chars, `src/transforms.js`) | yes | no | no (HMAC) |
| `format-preserving` | shape pseudonym | yes | no | no (documented as non-reversible) |
| `fake` | realistic fake name | yes | yes, but looks real | no |

A common use case needs something else: turn real documents (CVs, emails, chat transcripts, LLM request/response logs) into samples that can be shared, committed as test fixtures or sent to a model, where

- each entity becomes a typed, numbered placeholder: `Person-1`, `Person-2`, `Organization-1`, `Email-1`, `Phone-1`, `Location-1`, `Date-1`…;
- the same entity gets the same placeholder everywhere (across fields, records and files), so relations stay visible ("Person-1 worked at Organization-1 with Person-2");
- the owner can restore the original data later from a private map, and nobody else can.

## Proposal

1. **`placeholder` transformation**: `{mode: 'placeholder'}` replaces each personal finding with `<Type>-<n>`. Numbering is per type, in order of first appearance. Format configurable (`Person-1`, `[PERSON_1]`, `{{person_1}}`), with a check that the chosen format cannot collide with text already in the input.
2. **Private restore map**: the operation can return or write a map from placeholder to original value(s). Two serializations:
   - JSON;
   - [Links Notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation), e.g. `(Person-1: "Jane Doe")`.

   The map file is written with mode `0600`, never into the sanitized output, and is refused as an input to publication checks.
3. **Reuse a map**: passing an existing map continues it, so a corpus processed in several runs or files keeps `Person-1` meaning the same person, and new entities get the next free numbers.
4. **Restore**: `restore(text, map)` and `sensitive-data-sanitizer restore safe.txt --map map.lino`. It also works on text derived from the sanitized output, e.g. a model answer that quotes `Person-1`, which is the main reason to keep the map.
5. **Full anonymization**: the same mode with no map kept (`map: false`). The output is then irreversible: the numbering lives only in memory and is discarded, and residual verification runs as for `redact`.

## Details to decide

- **Variants of one entity.** `Jane Doe`, `J. Doe`, `Doe`, transliterations and inflected forms (Russian `Ивановым` / `Иванова`) should map to one placeholder. The existing component-identity logic of `fake` already links some of these. The map has to keep each original surface form so that restore gives back the exact original text, not a normalized one.
- **Structured input.** JSON/JSONL values and keys get the same placeholders as free text; the output must stay valid JSON.
- **Credentials.** Keep them fully redacted by default and never put them into the map unless explicitly requested.
- **Safety of the map.** Document clearly that the map is the personal data. The output alone is safe only to the extent detection is complete (see the coverage limits in the README).

## Acceptance

- Round trip: `restore(sanitize(text, {mode: 'placeholder'}).text, map) === text` for free text, JSON and JSONL fixtures, including inflected and transliterated names.
- Same entity in two files processed with one reused map gets the same placeholder.
- With `map: false`, no map is produced anywhere and the output passes residual verification.
- Both map formats parse back to the same map.

title: fix: Preserve Authorization boundaries and scale dense credential scans
body:
Authorization headers now preserve already-redacted tokens and angle placeholders, redact complete brace/square tokens, and leave NUL and other control bytes outside the credential. Dense Gitleaks matches now stop repeatedly copying the complete input into WASM after eight matches per rule/view and continue with the existing RE2JS engine.

- **#50:** fix the shared parser used by context and native Authorization detection. Cover Proxy-Authorization, multiple schemes, shell quotes, nested JSON escape depths, every C0 control and DEL, repeated sanitization, and exact binary output through CLI file/stdin with and without streaming.
- **#51:** apply the bounded fallback to every catalog rule. Preserve captures, entropy, anchors, UTF-16 offsets, complete long credentials, the existing large-view fallback, and the default Secretlint scanner union. Add a deterministic WASM-copy regression, a 256 KiB throughput regression, and finite reusable API/CLI benchmarks.
- Include one patch changeset for the automated release workflow and update API/coverage documentation.

The [complete requirement inventory, candidate solutions, primary-source library research, root causes and measurements](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-52-5379832e5bd4/docs/case-studies/issue-52/README.md) covers every requirement of the parent and both sub-issues. Both bugs reproduced before implementation; neither is deferred or classified as already resolved.

Reproduction and verification:

- `Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED] already` remains unchanged; `Authorization: Bearer {{token}} x` becomes `Authorization: [REDACTED] x`; `<token>` remains an exempt placeholder. `Authorization: Bearer abc\0 tail` becomes `Authorization: [REDACTED]\0 tail`, retaining the NUL byte.
- The original Authorization regression suite failed 17 of 21 tests. The original dense-input complexity regression failed too. The new regressions pass, including compilation of every vendored text rule in the fallback engine.
- At 64 KiB, the finite scanner comparison reduces whole-view WASM calls from **1,606 to 14** and local scanner time from **4.09 s to 0.16 s**. At 256 KiB, native verified sanitization takes **0.39 s**, and the default required scanner union and streaming each take **1.16 s**. Exact output is asserted; the existing fail-closed policy for oversized newline-only encoded containers is retained and documented.
- A cold CLI run with 6,400 distinct tokens (262,400 bytes) completes in **3.33 s** without streaming and **3.21 s** with streaming, including process startup and required scanners. Reproduce with `node --max-old-space-size=128 experiments/issue-52/cli-throughput.mjs` or use the API benchmark `node --max-old-space-size=256 --stack-size=4096 experiments/issue-52/dense-tokens.mjs 256`.
- Complete local suites: **Node 1,496 passing tests; Bun 1,496; Deno 1,351 plus eight steps**. The 256 KiB test takes 1.44 s in the full Node suite, 0.72 s in Bun and about 1 s in Deno. Runtimes run sequentially with bounded Node/Deno heaps.

Local lint, formatting, duplication, secrets, syntax, required docs, line limits, version and changeset checks pass. The existing Codex/Claude session corpus passes with one and four workers and zero residual secrets.

Implementation commit `704c4b7` passes [Checks and release](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/40068832000), including all **nine runtime/OS combinations**, [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/40068832006), [Example app](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/40068832089), and [link checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/40068832054). title: Dense credentials take quadratic time: every re2-wasm exec copies the whole view (256 KiB of ghp_ tokens: 72 s)
body:
## Summary

Sanitizing text with many credential matches takes quadratic time in 0.12.1. Each `RE2#exec` call of re2-wasm copies the whole scanned view into WASM again, and gitleaks rules call `exec` once per match.

- 128 KiB of `ghp_` tokens takes about 18 s.
- 256 KiB takes 72 s, about 3.6 KB/s.
- Plain log text of the same size takes about 1 s.

#47 sped up ordinary large logs. This case is separate: it scales with the number of matches.

## Reproduction

`@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer` 0.12.1, Node.js 22, Linux x64. Each test file is newline-separated random `ghp_` + 36 alphanumerics, sanitized with `redact - --credentials-only --allow-binary` (with or without `--stream`, same result):

| Input                                         | Time        |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| 32 KiB of tokens                              | 2.1 s       |
| 64 KiB of tokens                              | 5.4–6.0 s   |
| 128 KiB of tokens                             | 17.7–19.3 s |
| 256 KiB of tokens (one line, space-separated) | 72.5 s      |
| 64 KiB of git SHAs / base64 / UUIDs           | about 1.0 s |
| 300 KB of ordinary log lines                  | 1.7 s       |

Each doubling of the input roughly triples or quadruples the time. Line breaks don't matter: 128 KiB with one token per line takes 18.6 s.

Script: [experiments/issue-253/sanitizer-findings.sh](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/issue-253-480126f69838/experiments/issue-253/sanitizer-findings.sh)

## Cause

`node --cpu-prof` on the 64 KiB input shows the time going to `exec` in `src/re2.js`, called from `ruleMatches` in `src/gitleaks.js:157`:

```
1666 ms  wasm-function[72]   exec@src/re2.js < ruleMatches@src/gitleaks.js:157 < scanRule < detectGitleaks
 519 ms  stringToUTF8Array   toWireType < exec@src/re2.js < ruleMatches ...
 334 ms  lengthBytesUTF8     toWireType < exec@src/re2.js < ruleMatches ...
```

`ruleMatches` loops `pattern.exec(text)` with `lastIndex`. Every call converts the full `text` to UTF-8 and copies it into the WASM heap (`toWireType`), then searches from `lastIndex`. With N matches in a view of L bytes, that is O(N·L) work for each rule that matches.

## Suggested fix

Any of these would make it linear:

- Run the RE2JS path that `large` views already use (no copy into WASM) once a view has produced more than a few matches.
- Or scan bounded windows around each rule keyword hit (gitleaks rules carry `keywords`) instead of the whole view.
- Or copy the view into WASM once and search it with offsets, if re2-wasm can be driven that way.

Please add a throughput test with a dense-token input, for example 256 KiB of `ghp_` tokens under a few seconds.

title: Authorization tokens end at "]" or "}" and swallow a following NUL: "Bearer [REDACTED]" becomes "[REDACTED]]"
body:
## Summary

In 0.12.1 the token of an `Authorization: <scheme> <token>` header ends at the first `]` or `}`, and it does not end at a NUL byte. As a result:

- Sanitizing an already sanitized log is not idempotent: `Bearer [REDACTED]` becomes `[REDACTED]]`.
- Template placeholders leave their closing brackets behind: `Bearer {{token}}` becomes `[REDACTED]}}`.
- With `--allow-binary`, a NUL right after the token is masked along with it, so the output no longer keeps every non-secret byte.

Found while moving start-command to 0.12.1, which dropped its own Authorization pre-pass now that #45 is fixed (link-foundation/start#253). start sanitizes terminal transcripts, and those often hold logs that were already sanitized.

## Reproduction

`@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer` 0.12.1, Node.js 22, run with `redact - --credentials-only --allow-binary`:

| Input                                      | Output                                | Expected                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED] already` | `Authorization: [REDACTED]] already`  | `Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED] already` (or `[REDACTED] already`)    |
| `Authorization: Bearer {{token}} x`        | `Authorization: [REDACTED]}} x`       | `Authorization: [REDACTED] x` (or the placeholder kept, like `<token>`) |
| `Authorization: Bearer <token> x`          | `Authorization: [REDACTED] <token> x` | (consistent, for comparison)                                            |
| `Authorization: Bearer abc\0 tail`         | `Authorization: [REDACTED] tail`      | `Authorization: [REDACTED]\0 tail`                                      |

```sh
printf 'Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED] already\n' | sensitive-data-sanitizer redact - --credentials-only
printf 'Authorization: Bearer abc\0 tail\n' | sensitive-data-sanitizer redact - --credentials-only --allow-binary | od -c
```

A NUL after a non-Authorization credential is kept (`ghp_…\0` becomes `[REDACTED]\0`), so only the Authorization path is affected.

Script: [experiments/issue-253/sanitizer-findings.sh](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/issue-253-480126f69838/experiments/issue-253/sanitizer-findings.sh)

## Cause

`authorizationRange` in `src/context.js`:

```js
if (text.startsWith(REDACTED, start)) {
  return undefined;
}
const match = /^(?:[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*[ \t]+)?[^\s"'\\,<>}\]]+/i.exec(
  text.slice(start)
);
```

- The `REDACTED` guard runs only before the scheme, so `Bearer [REDACTED]` slips past it. The token class then stops at `]` and masks `[REDACTED`.
- `}` and `]` end the token even when the token itself opened the bracket (`{{token}}`, `[REDACTED]`).
- `\0` and other C0 control bytes are not in the excluded class, so they become part of the token.

## Suggested fix

- Also skip, or keep unchanged, a token that starts with `[REDACTED]` after the scheme.
- When a token starts with `{`, `[` or `<`, end it at the matching closing bracket, or treat it as a placeholder the way `<token>` already is. Do not cut it at the first closing bracket.
- Add `\0` (`\x00-\x1f`) to the excluded class.
- Add the four rows above to the test suite.

title: fix: Bound Authorization redaction and unblock large log streams
body:
Authorization headers now redact the scheme and one credential token while preserving the rest of shell commands and escaped JSON log lines. Authentication configuration variables no longer erase ordinary host names throughout a log. Large file streams renew their worker deadline after completed batches and accept an explicit opt-in for NUL bytes.

- **#45:** share Authorization range parsing between context and native detection. Stop at whitespace, quotes, backslashes and commas; retain credential-reference exemptions, Proxy-Authorization support, and all other detectors.
- **#46:** exclude authentication configuration suffixes such as AUTH_TRANSPORT, AUTH_MODE and AUTH_METHOD during automatic environment discovery. Explicit selections still work, and short, URL-shaped and path-shaped real credentials remain eligible.
- **#47:** expose `--worker-timeout-ms N`, preserve a finite inactivity deadline for file workers and a per-batch deadline for JSONL workers, and support `allowBinary: true` / `--allow-binary` across plain log paths. Structured data and configuration remain strict. Replace the measured escaped-string regex hotspot with a bounded linear scanner; retain fresh residual verification and the complete scanner union.
- Refresh vulnerable transitive lockfile entries that failed the initial security workflow, and add one patch changeset for release.

The [complete requirement inventory, alternative solutions, primary-source research and verification evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-48-91ec9d5d4db8/docs/case-studies/issue-48/README.md) cover every parent requirement and all three required sub-issues. title: Large logs: file mode stops at the 60 s worker deadline (ERR_WORKER), one NUL byte blocks the log (ERR_BINARY), ~1 MB/s
body:
Large and real-world logs are blocked or slow with 0.12.0 `redact --stream --credentials-only`.

1. **File mode stops at the 60 s worker deadline.** `redact <file> --stream --output <out>` uses `sanitizeFileBounded` with `workerTimeoutMs ?? 60000` (`src/stream.js:397`), and the CLI has no option to change it. An 80 MB synthetic log fails after 61 s with `ERR_WORKER`. Stdin mode (`redact - --stream --output <out> < file`) completes the same file in 208 s, which is about 0.4 MB/s for this log (it has one 15 MB escaped-JSON line). Callers that need to finish have to use stdin mode.
2. **One NUL byte blocks the whole log** with `ERR_BINARY` (`src/stream.js:248`):
   ```
   $ printf 'line one\n\0line two\n' | sensitive-data-sanitizer redact - --credentials-only --stream --output out.log
   Sanitization failed; output was blocked (ERR_BINARY).
   ```
   Terminal transcripts sometimes contain NUL bytes. Failing closed is safe, but an opt-in such as `--allow-binary`, which treats NUL as an ordinary byte, would let these logs be published.
3. **Throughput.** Ordinary log text runs at about 1 MB/s, and CLI startup takes about 4 s. A 100 MB execution log therefore takes minutes.

Reproduction script: https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/issue-251-cce19f18f1c5/experiments/issue-251/upstream-repro.sh (with `make-large-log.js` next to it).

Output from `LARGE_MIB=80 experiments/issue-251/upstream-repro.sh`:
```
Sanitization failed; output was blocked (ERR_WORKER).
file mode exit=2 seconds=61
stdin mode exit=0 seconds=208
```

title: --env-secrets masks configuration values of AUTH-named variables (GIT_AUTH_TRANSPORT=github.com masks every github.com)
body:
`--env-secrets` takes the value of every variable whose name matches `src/known.js` `secretEnvName`, including `AUTH` as a name part. Some of those values are configuration, not secrets, and masking them removes ordinary log content everywhere. Version 0.12.0:

```
$ printf 'git remote: https://github.com/owner/repo\n' |
  env GIT_AUTH_TRANSPORT=github.com sensitive-data-sanitizer redact - --credentials-only --env-secrets
git remote: https://[REDACTED]/owner/repo
```

A real case is the hive-mind host, which sets `HIVE_MIND_GIT_AUTH_TRANSPORT=github.com`. Every `github.com` in an uploaded log is masked there.

Possible fixes:
- skip values that look like host names, URLs, paths, booleans or short words;
- require a minimum length or entropy for literal env values;
- add an exclusion list for names such as `*_AUTH_TRANSPORT`, `*_AUTH_MODE` and `*_AUTH_METHOD` (similar to the `auth_mode` values in #40).

start-command used the same name rule before it moved to this library (link-foundation/start#250). The behavior is not new, but it now lives in one place.

title: Authorization header values that are not double-quoted are masked to the end of the line
body:
`Authorization` header values that are not double-quoted are masked to the end of the line, so the rest of the line is lost. Version 0.12.0, `redact - --credentials-only`:

```
$ printf '%s\n' \
  'curl -H "Authorization: token ghx1234567890abcdefXYZ" keep-after' \
  "curl -H 'Authorization: token ghx1234567890abcdefXYZ' keep-after" \
  'Authorization: Bearer abc.def.ghi keep-after' |
  sensitive-data-sanitizer redact - --credentials-only
curl -H "Authorization: [REDACTED]" keep-after
curl -H 'Authorization: [REDACTED]
Authorization: [REDACTED]
```

`inspect()` shows which rules match:

```
"curl -H 'Authorization: token ghx1234567890abcdefXYZ' keep-after"
    context "token ghx1234567890abcdefXYZ' keep-after"
    gitleaks/curl-auth-header "ghx1234567890abcdefXYZ"
"Authorization: Bearer abc.def.ghi keep-after"
    context "Bearer abc.def.ghi keep-after"
    authorization "abc.def.ghi keep-after"
```

- `src/detection.js:191` `/(?:Proxy-)?Authorization[ \t]*:[ \t]*(?:Bearer|Basic|Digest)[ \t]+([^\r\n"',]+)/gi` does not stop at whitespace.
- The `context` rule (`src/context.js`, key `authorization`) takes everything up to the end of the line after a single quote or no quote at all.

This matters for logs that contain a long single-line JSON request body, where a header can appear inside a prompt. That is the case in link-foundation/start#249, where 2.9 MB of a 4.5 MB log was dropped. Expected: mask the scheme and one token, stopping at whitespace, a quote, `\` or `,`, as the double-quoted case already does.

start-command keeps a small pre-pass for now (`js/src/lib/log-sanitizer.js`, `AuthorizationHeaderMask`). It masks `Authorization: <scheme> <token>` before calling the CLI, and can be removed once this is fixed.

title: feat: Unify tool-log sanitization and remove large-input bottlenecks
body:
Tool logs currently lose benign auth/package metadata, reject malformed UTF-8 and long records, and can take minutes on image-bearing lines. This change fixes the shared API, CLI, structured and streaming paths and adds the integration options needed by gh-upload-log, start-command and hive-mind.

Fixes #43
Fixes #40
Fixes #41
Fixes #42

### Requirements and implementation

- Preserve the reported disk paths, local IPs, auth modes, literal gh/Actions credential references, Actions permissions, npm dependency names/versions and token counts under the default scanner union. Real credential controls still redact.
- Remove repeated-prefix regex scans, V8 stack overflow and repeated WASM copies. Keep the complete Gitleaks catalog; use RE2JS for large inputs to avoid the fixed WASM heap. Required context/prefix views preserve complete credential matches and Unicode offsets.
- Preserve invalid log bytes reversibly through whole files, stdin, atomic output, workers and both streaming passes. JSON/JSONL, configuration and scanner protocols retain strict text validation.
- Discover values from credential-named environment variables without a manual name list; retain explicit selection. Add opt-in collection from every host/account in gh's hosts.yml using bounded YAML parsing.
- Add credentialsOnly / --credentials-only across the finding policy, including encoded, external, structured and stream paths. Preserve public account details while continuing credential detection.
- Accept long plain-text logical records up to the configured total input budget, including credentials spanning many 64 KiB chunks. Keep explicit record/total/worker limits and atomic publication. Raise the whole-input default to 32 MiB.
- Include a packed shared-tool integration example, public API/types, documentation and one minor Changeset. Refresh compatible root/example lockfile dependencies to resolve existing security audit failures. Prepare Deno dependencies separately from its unchanged test execution budget.

The [complete requirement inventory, alternatives, research and root causes](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-43-840a44177950/docs/case-studies/issue-43/ANALYSIS.md) maps every requirement in #40–#43 to implementation and verification. Consumer migrations remain tracked in gh-upload-log#55, start#250 and link-assistant/hive-mind#3740.

### Reproduction and verification

New regressions first reproduced benign-log redaction, ERR_ENCODING on invalid bytes and ERR_LIMIT on a >1 MiB header. Tests cover sync/default async/JSONL parity, real credential controls, every byte/chunk split, worker/two-pass publication, env discovery, YAML failure modes, credentials-only filtering and differential vendored-rule matches.

Finite seeded 15.7 MB probes completed in 11.2 seconds for repeated A, 11.1 seconds for zero-filled base64 and 34.1 seconds for random base64, using a 256 MiB JS heap. The earlier 25 KB repeated-A reproduction took 6.2 seconds. Reusable probes and profiles are retained in experiments/issue-43. These are container measurements, not fixed latency guarantees.

Runtime results, clean-tarball installation checks and final CI evidence are recorded in [VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-43-840a44177950/docs/case-studies/issue-43/VALIDATION.md).

- Local suites: Node 1,399/1,399; final Bun 1,399/1,399; final Deno 1,254/1,254 plus eight steps. The final focused Node suite passes 91 tests, and the write-enabled Deno regressions pass 28 tests.
- Local lint, formatting, duplication, secrets, syntax, documentation, file-limit and Changeset/version guards pass. Both npm audits report zero vulnerabilities. A clean consumer installation of the packed tarball verifies API exports and both CLI entry points.
- [Implementation-head CI](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/39999201490) passes all nine Node/Bun/Deno jobs across Ubuntu, macOS and Windows, plus Docker and integration checks. All five workflows passed on implementation commit `6d7994b` (38 successful checks, 10 conditional skips).
- Final documentation commit `c316fc5` passes all applicable checks: [Checks and release](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/40000062772), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/40000062731), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/40000062898), [Example app](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/40000062740), [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/40000063093). Runtime jobs are conditionally skipped for this documentation-only follow-up; implementation files are unchanged from the fully tested commit.

### Required outcome still blocked: npm publication

**Do not merge while actual publication remains unfinished.** npm returns E404 for the package, GitHub has no release, repository Actions secrets are empty, and no local publishing credential is available. Main release [38456752244](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/38456752244) reports an npm OIDC exchange 404 and no NPM_TOKEN fallback (log lines 153–160). Passing CI and the clean local packed-install smoke test do not constitute publication.

A package owner must establish the npm trusted publisher for this repository's release.yml or supply a scoped bootstrap NPM_TOKEN. Then run the release workflow, verify registry installation and both API/CLI entry points, and confirm the GitHub release. Existing PR preflight remains advisory; main retains the explicit actionable failure. This external acceptance criterion is left unfinished.

title: Become the one sanitizer for gh-upload-log, start-command and hive-mind: publish to npm, and take over their practices (environment secrets, gh hosts.yml, non-UTF-8 bytes, unbounded lines, credentials-only mode)
body:
The maintainer wants one sanitizer for all our tools: link-foundation/gh-upload-log, link-foundation/start (`$ --upload-log`) and link-assistant/hive-mind should all use this library, and this library should take the best practices of all three. Today none of them depends on it, and each has its own rules.

Compared on 2026-10-23 (this repository 02104ac, start-command 0.39.1 main, hive-mind 2.39.6 main, gh-upload-log 0.12.1 main):

1. **Publish to npm.** `npm view @link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer` returns E404, and there are no GitHub releases (#23, #28 were closed). The three tools cannot depend on it until it is published.
2. **Secret values from the environment, without listing names by hand.**
   - start-command masks the exact value of every environment variable whose name matches `/(?:^|_)(?:TOKEN|(?:API|ACCESS|PRIVATE)?KEY|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|CREDENTIALS?|AUTH|PAT)(?:_|$)/i`.
   - hive-mind keeps a curated list of AI-tool variables (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `CODEX_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`, `HF_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, …, `src/token-sanitization.lib.mjs` `KNOWN_LOCAL_TOKEN_ENV_VARS`).
   - Here, `knownSecretsFromEnv` reads only explicitly named variables. Test: `MY_SERVICE_TOKEN=<value>` in the environment, and the same value in the input is kept.
3. **Local credential files.** hive-mind also reads GitHub tokens from `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`, not only from `gh auth token`.
4. **Bytes that are not UTF-8** are kept by start-command (Latin-1 mapping), while this library blocks the whole output: see the encoding part of #41.
5. **Unbounded lines.** start-command streams in 64 KB blocks and keeps a continuation state, so a token or header longer than a block cannot leak its tail. hive-mind holds back up to 8 MB (`DEFAULT_MAX_HOLD_BYTES`). Here `--max-record-bytes` is 1 MB for text, and longer lines are slow (#41).
6. **Keep public account details.** For our logs, the maintainer: "Account details is public, not a leak." and "github.com/konard is public account." A tool should be able to run credentials-only (no personal-data replacement), or keep every EMAIL and account-ID finding of a stated list, without one `publicEntities` entry per value and a review date each.
7. **The false positives already fixed elsewhere**, see #40: hive-mind's npm package-name exemption (link-assistant/hive-mind#2156) and token-count exemption (link-assistant/hive-mind#2119; already correct here).

gh-upload-log has no sanitizer at all today, so for it this library would be the first one.


The moves are tracked in link-foundation/gh-upload-log#55, link-foundation/start#250 and link-assistant/hive-mind#3740.

title: Long log lines are slow (runs of one character are quadratic: 100 KB 28 s, 1.5 MB > 9 min; base64 ~20 s/MB) and invalid UTF-8 blocks the whole output
body:
Logs from AI tools have very long single lines: escaped JSON request bodies (100 KB and more), and Codex rollouts with base64 images (one line is 3.6 MB on average and up to 15.7 MB). Measured with commit 02104ac, `redact --native-only --output`, on a MacBook:

| Input (one line) | Size | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `A` repeated | 25 KB | 1.95 s |
| `A` repeated | 50 KB | 7.17 s |
| `A` repeated | 100 KB | 28.24 s |
| `A` repeated | 1.5 MB | stopped after 9 min of CPU |
| random base64 in JSON | 100 KB | 1.33 s |
| random base64 in JSON | 1 MB | 19.72 s |
| base64 with zero-filled runs (like a PNG) | 1 MB | 12.05 s |
| 120,000 ordinary log lines, `--stream` | 14 MB | 7.24 s |

Time grows quadratically with the length of a run of one character, and about 20 s per MB for base64 lines. Base64 PNG data has long `AAAA…` runs wherever the image has flat areas.

Reproduce: `python3 -c "print('A'*100000)" > l.log; time node bin/sensitive-data-sanitizer.js redact l.log --native-only --output l.out`

Invalid UTF-8 also blocks the whole output:

```
printf 'ok line\n\xff\xfe invalid utf8 \xc3\x28 here\nsecond\n' > bad.log
node bin/sensitive-data-sanitizer.js redact bad.log --native-only
Sanitization failed; output was blocked (ERR_ENCODING).
```

Terminal logs often contain such bytes (binary output, cut multibyte characters). Blocking means the log is never published. start-command's sanitizer maps bytes through Latin-1 and keeps them (`src/lib/log-sanitizer.js`, "Latin-1 provides a reversible byte mapping, including invalid UTF-8").

Expected: linear time on long lines, so a 15 MB line finishes in seconds; invalid bytes are kept as they are (or replaced in a lossless way) while the valid text around them is still sanitized.

title: False positives in tool logs: `sk-` inside words (`disk-baseline-…`), loopback and private IPs, `auth_mode`/`auth_method` values and shell expressions, package names, GitHub Actions `id-token`/`${{ secrets.X }}`
body:
Found while checking which sanitizer to use for hive-mind, start-command and gh-upload-log logs. Commit 02104ac (0.11.31), `redact --native-only` and default, same result. All inputs below are synthetic.

```
Command: gate='/tmp/hive-mind-disk-baseline-0ce9e170-e6d3-494d-91e1-0d820245d34b'
🧠 Formal AI: endpoint http://172.18.0.2:8080/api/openai/v1
proxy example: "socks5://127.0.0.1:1080"
INFO codex_otel.log_only: event.name="codex.conversation_starts" auth_mode="Chatgpt"
auth_method: "oauth"
use: curl -L -H "Authorization: token $(gh auth token)" -o <filename> <url>
  "devDependencies": { "secretlint": "^9.0.0", "next-auth": "^5.0.0", "@secretlint/secretlint-rule-preset-recommend": "^9.0.0" }
permissions:
  id-token: write
  token: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

Output:

```
Command: gate='/tmp/hive-mind-di[REDACTED]'
🧠 Formal AI: endpoint http://[REDACTED]:8080/api/openai/v1
proxy example: "socks5://[REDACTED]:1080"
INFO codex_otel.log_only: event.name="codex.conversation_starts" auth_mode="[REDACTED]"
auth_method: "[REDACTED]"
use: curl -L -H "Authorization: [REDACTED]" -o <filename> <url>
  "devDependencies": { "secretlint": "[REDACTED]", "next-auth": "[REDACTED]", "[REDACTED]/secretlint-rule-preset-recommend": "[REDACTED]" }
permissions:
  id-token: [REDACTED]
  token: [REDACTED]
```

None of these values is a secret.

1. `openai` rule, `src/rules.js:14`: `/sk-(?:proj-|svcacct-|admin-)?[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}/g` has no left boundary, so it matches inside `disk-baseline-<uuid>` (every hive-mind execution log has this line). start-command has the same bug: link-foundation/start#249.
2. `ipv4`: loopback `127.0.0.1` and private `172.18.0.2`, `10.0.0.5`, `192.168.1.10` are redacted as personal data, while `8.8.8.8` is kept. Loopback, RFC 1918 and Docker bridge addresses identify no one.
3. `context` (SECRET): a value under an `auth*` key is masked even when it is a mode or method name (`Chatgpt`, `oauth`, `ApiKey`) or a shell expression (`$(gh auth token)`), which is the hive-mind system prompt text.
4. Package manifests: dependency names containing `secret` / `auth` and their version ranges are masked. hive-mind already exempts them (link-assistant/hive-mind#2156).
5. GitHub Actions: `id-token: write` is a permission, and `${{ secrets.X }}` is a reference, not a value. Reported for hive-mind in link-assistant/hive-mind#2841.

Expected: all lines above are unchanged, and regression tests cover them. The real credential cases keep working, for example `Authorization: token 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567` is redacted, which this library already does correctly (hive-mind currently does not).

title: fix: bound credential label values and redact residuals to a fixed point
body:
Fixes #38.

Credential-label spans no longer block session publication. Prose such as `token for ES.`, `SIG for\n:sig is d` and `token for\\ery record … request-log write lock` stays unchanged. A quoted `sig:'` value never reaches the following JSON keys. `APIkey="\"private_key:9"` is published as `APIkey="[REDACTED]"`.

- **Label boundaries:** credential qualifiers (`for/от/для/…`) stay on one logical line. They cannot cross escaped `\n`, escape sequences or quotes. Verbs such as `is/es/est` are whole words, so `request` no longer ends in the verb `est`.
- **Generic labels in prose:** `token`, `sig`, `secret`, `cookie` and similar labels followed by a verb need a generated-looking value. Password-family and compound labels (`the password is hunter2`, `api key is …`) are unchanged.
- **Values never include JSON keys:** quoted values are bounded by the enclosing JSON string, including strings at the start of a structured batch line.
- **Same encoding layer:** a credential covering a whole escaped JSON run is redacted as one value, instead of re-encoding a sanitized copy that lost its label. Base64 payloads under `preserveEncoding` are still re-encoded.
- **Fixed-point re-redaction:** when verification still finds a value, the output is redacted again for up to three rounds (`residualRounds`). Each round emits a value-free `residual-redaction` debug event. Output that does not converge still fails with `ERR_RESIDUAL`, and structured JSON verification still runs on the final text. The sync and async paths share `redactAgain`.
- **Corpus, docs, release:** the issue records are added to the Codex/Claude publication corpus. The PR also adds a patch Changeset, API documentation, a case study (`docs/case-studies/issue-38-credential-labels/README.md`), and experiments in `experiments/issue-38/`.

### Reproduction

```sh
node experiments/issue-38/reproduce.mjs          # main: ERR_JSON_COLLISION + 4× ERR_RESIDUAL
node experiments/issue-38/fuzz.mjs 3000 1         # main: 23/3000 blocked (19 collision, 4 residual)
node --test --test-timeout=30000 tests/sanitizer-issue-38.test.js   # main: 28/36 fail
node --max-old-space-size=512 experiments/issue-34/session-corpus.mjs  # main: ERR_JSON_COLLISION
```

### Tests

`tests/sanitizer-issue-38.test.js` has 36 tests:
- Every issue record goes through `sanitize`, `createSanitizer().sanitize`, `sanitizeJsonl`, and `sanitizeStreamToFile` with `twoPass` false and true.
- Prose label boundaries must stay unchanged.
- Credential values must still be redacted in plain and JSONL text, with keys preserved.
- Fixed-point redaction is checked in the sync and async engines, and a non-converging detector must still fail closed.

One existing expectation changed. `sanitizer-stream-identity.test.js` ("never reuses coordinator findings for residual verification") now expects the fresh verifier's late finding to be redacted rather than raise `ERR_RESIDUAL`. Its detector also returns no finding once the value is gone. This matches the issue's request for fixed-point re-redaction.

### Validation

- Node 1,355 / 1,355, Bun 1,355 / 1,355, Deno 1,210 + 8 steps.
- `npm run check` (lint, format, duplication) and the file line limits pass.
- The extended session corpus has zero residuals with 1 and 4 workers.
- Fuzz: 0 failures with seeds 1, 7 and 99 at 8,000 records each, and no residual rounds were needed.

### Assumptions and limits

- The private 911-session corpus was not supplied, so these results give no new pass rate for it.
- A short dictionary word after a generic label and a verb (`the token is valid`) is treated as text. Use `knownSecrets` to redact such a value when it really is a credential.

title: After #37: 782/911 real sessions publish; remaining 129 blocked by SECRET/context label spans (prose 'token for', JSON keys after 'sig:')
body:
## Summary

Re-verification of #36 after PR #37 (`main` @ `edb778f`). All #36 reproductions and the `tel:` / `Fax:` leak are fixed. On the same real public-repository sessions, **782 of 911** now publish, up from 418:

| Result | After #35 | After #37 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| OK | 418 | **782** |
| `ERR_RESIDUAL` | 369 | 124 |
| `ERR_JSON_COLLISION` | 42 | 5 |
| `ERR_JSON` / `ERR_ENCODING` / `ERR_LATE_PERSONAL` / `ERR_FINDING` | 82 | **0** |

By source: Codex 672 of 765, Claude Code 110 of 146. Options: `{ structured: 'jsonl', profile: 'publication', twoPass: true, workers: 1 }`.

An independent leak audit of the 782 passing outputs found no leaks. It checked MRZ (with check digits), RU passport, SNILS and INN (checksums), PNR, ticket, visa, DOB, card (Luhn), IBAN, phone, `tel:`, email, IPv4, provider tokens, JWT, private keys, URL credentials and home paths. All remaining hits were false positives in the audit itself (UUID fragments, `noreply@github.com`, `/Users/runner/`, `{api_key}` placeholders).

The 129 remaining failures fail closed. Nothing leaks, but those sessions cannot be published. In every minimized case the cause is the **`SECRET/context` credential-label rule**, which has the same flaw #34 fixed for personal labels: a `token` / `sig` / `key` label word in prose captures text after it across escaped newlines, or captures JSON keys.

## Reproductions

Each one was minimized automatically from a real failing session, and none contains private data. Each fails in `sanitize`, `sanitizeJsonl` and `sanitizeStreamToFile` (one-pass and two-pass):

```js
sanitize(text, { profile: 'publication', structured: 'jsonl' });
```

### 1. `ERR_JSON_COLLISION`: `sig:` captures following JSON keys

```jsonl
{"payload":{"content":[{"text":"sig:' "},{"type":"","text":""}]}}
```

`SECRET/context` reports `sig:' `, then `type` and `text`, which are **object keys** of the next array element. Redacted: `{"[REDACTED]":"","[REDACTED]":""}`.

### 2. `ERR_RESIDUAL`: prose after `token for` / `SIG for` across `\n`

```jsonl
{"toolUseResult":{"stdout":"token for ES.\nes u"}}
{"toolUseResult":{"stdout":"SIG for\n:sig is d"}}
{"payload":{"content":[{"text":"token for\\ery record. The enclosing request-log write lock serio\\n/// this c"}]}}
```

Findings and redacted output:
- `"u"` → `token for ES[REDACTED]\nes u`. The redaction lands on `.`, and verification then finds `u` again.
- `"sig is d"` and `"d"` → `:sig is [REDACTED]`. Verification finds `sig is [REDACTED]` as a new secret.
- `"-log write lock serio"` → only `c` is redacted, and verification finds the same span again.

In all three, the span that detection reports differs from the span that redaction replaces (raw vs. decoded offsets), so verification sees the "secret" again. The values are ordinary English words, so they should not be detected at all. `token for`, `SIG for` and `sig is` are prose, not `key: value` assignments.

### 3. `ERR_RESIDUAL`: nested escaped quotes in a key assignment

```jsonl
{"payload":{"content":[{"text":"APIkey=\"\\\"private_key:9\""}]}}
```

`SECRET/context` reports both `\\\"private_key:9` and `9`. Redaction then throws `ERR_RESIDUAL`, presumably because the outer and inner findings overlap across escape layers.

## Expected

- Credential labels in prose (`token for`, `sig is`, `SIG for`) are not assignments. A `SECRET/context` value must follow `:` or `=` directly on the same logical line, must stop at escaped `\n` or a closing quote (as #35 did for personal labels), and must never include JSON keys or structural characters.
- When `structured` is set, the detection and redaction spans for `SECRET/context` use the same encoding layer, so verification cannot find the same span again.
- If a value is still detected after redaction, it is redacted again (fixed-point), not reported as a hard failure, as long as the output stays valid JSON.
- Add these record shapes to the publication corpus.

Related: #34, #36, #37. npm publication is still tracked in #28: `npm view sensitive-data-sanitizer` still returns 404.

title: fix: preserve structured session metadata and normalize two-pass identities
body:
Fixes #36.

Session publication now preserves `null`, rate-limit keys, Rust paths, Claude tool schemas, and jq expressions from the reported reproductions. National `tel:` links, fax numbers, and Vietnamese `ĐT` labels are redacted, and escaped public names and credential headers publish without residual or encoding errors.

- Require plausible person/place values before personal labels establish propagation seeds. Confine inferred structured propagation to string values and keep registry matches distinct from explicit private values.
- Apply public policy to decoded detection, stop credential spans at escaped delimiters, and preserve surrounding command text.
- Trim stream confirmations consistently and reserve `ERR_LATE_PERSONAL` for one-pass publication. Two-pass redaction accepts additional confirmations while retaining limits and residual verification.
- Add the minimized issue cases and actual Codex `turn_context` / `rate_limits` and Claude `attachment.tools` / `wireToolInputs` / `toolUseResult` records to the existing CI corpus. Add a patch Changeset and API documentation.

Reproduce with `node --max-old-space-size=512 experiments/issue-36/reproduce.mjs`. The initial regression suite failed 56 of 63 tests against the original implementation. Automated coverage now checks native and required-engine sanitization, atomic two-pass output with one/four workers, structured boundaries, whitespace normalization, additional second-pass confirmations, public/private policy, and real escaped credentials.

Validation:

- Full runtime suites passed: Node 1,319 tests, Bun 1,319 tests, Deno 1,174 tests plus eight steps (CI permissions; filesystem publication paths run in Node/Bun).
- Focused regressions and existing context, catalog, encoding, and stream checks passed.
- Extended Codex/Claude corpus: all four one/four-worker publications passed with valid JSON and zero residual findings.
- Lint, formatting, duplication, secret scan, syntax, file limits, documentation, version, and Changeset checks passed.
- Hosted Node/Bun/Deno tests passed on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows: [full implementation matrix](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/38300251805).

Detailed reproduction and root-cause evidence: [case study](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-36-581486aaaa3f/docs/case-studies/issue-36-session-publication/README.md).

title: Real sessions still blocked after #35: name/state labels confirm code tokens and propagation rewrites raw JSON; twoPass still throws ERR_LATE_PERSONAL
body: ## Summary Re-verification of #34 after PR #35 (`main` @ `ada53fd`). The #34 reproductions are fixed, and the Codex Guardian prompt no longer crashes. Real sessions are still mostly blocked, though: **418 of 911** public-repository session files (≤ 5 MB) publish. Claude Code sessions are hit hardest, with only **9 of 146** passing. Every failure is fail-closed, so nothing leaked. The main root cause is the `name` / `state` catalog labels confirming arbitrary code tokens as personal values. Propagation then rewrites those tokens everywhere in the **raw JSON text**: JSON literals, keys and structural characters. Options used for every run: ```js await sanitizeStreamToFile(createReadStream(file), out, { structured: 'jsonl', profile: 'publication', twoPass: true, workers: 1, }); ``` | Result | Files (after #33) | Files (after #35) | | --- | ---: | ---: | | OK | 20 | **418** | | `SyntaxError` (raw) | 818 | 0 | | `ERR_RESIDUAL` | 49 | **369** | | `ERR_JSON_COLLISION` | 18 | 42 | | `ERR_ENCODING` | 2 | 36 | | `ERR_JSON` | 0 | 32 | | `ERR_LATE_PERSONAL` (with `twoPass: true`) | 6 | 10 | | `ERR_FINDING` | 0 | 4 | By source: Codex 409 of 765 OK, Claude Code 9 of 146 OK. (Two files from the earlier 913 were deleted locally in between. Three `ERR_OUTPUT` results were my harness reusing an existing target path; those files pass.) Throughput is much better: 129 MB of passing sessions took about 5,000 worker-seconds (about 0.026 MB/s per worker), and most files finish in seconds. Every reproduction below was minimized automatically from a real failing session, keeping only records and characters that are needed. None of them contains private data. Each one fails on its own as a JSONL file: ```js import { sanitize } from 'sensitive-data-sanitizer'; sanitize(text, { profile: 'publication', structured: 'jsonl' }); // and/or sanitizeStreamToFile(Readable.from([text]), out, { structured: 'jsonl', profile: 'publication', twoPass: true }) ``` ## 1. `name:` / `name=` confirms any following token as a person, then propagation rewrites raw JSON `PERSON/catalog/aws` and `PERSON/label` accept whatever follows `name:` or `name=`, including `null`, `codec`, `Coding`, `Claude`, `...`, `name` and `:{`. `document-propagation` then replaces every occurrence of that value in the raw JSONL text, outside string values as well. ### 1a. `ERR_JSON`: the JSON literal `null` is rewritten ```jsonl {"payload":{"collaboration_mode":{"settings":{"developer_instructions":null}}}} {"payload":{"content":[{"text":"name:null"}]}} ``` Redacted text: `"developer_instructions":[REDACTED]}`, which is invalid JSON. Every Codex `turn_context` record contains `null` literals, so any later `name:null` blocks the whole session. ### 1b. `ERR_JSON`: structural characters are rewritten (`nom:` label) ```jsonl {"payload":{"content":[{"text":"nom::{\\n"}]}} ``` `nom:` (Rust parser combinator crate, `nom::{...}`) is read as a name label with value `:{`. Redacted text: `{"payload"[REDACTED]"content":...`. ### 1c. `ERR_JSON_COLLISION`: key `limit_name` collides after propagating `name` ```jsonl {"payload":{"rate_limits":{"limit_id":"","limit_name":null}}} {"payload":{"content":[{"text":"name=name"},{"text":"id\"name:\"C"}]}} ``` This is the standard Codex `rate_limits` record shape. Fails in stream mode (two-pass: `ERR_JSON_COLLISION`; one-pass: `ERR_RESIDUAL`). ### 1d. `ERR_RESIDUAL`: propagated code tokens leave `::`, which the IPv6 rule then flags ```jsonl {"payload":{"content":[{"text":"name=codec"}]}} {"payload":{"content":[{"text":"codec::"}]}} ``` ```jsonl {"payload":{"content":[{"text":"ai\"name:\"Coding"},{"text":"a::coding_"}]}} ``` After redaction: `[REDACTED]::` and `a::[REDACTED]_`, which give a residual `IP_ADDRESS/ipv6` on `::` and `a::`. Rust paths (`codec::`, `serde_json::`, `a::b`) are everywhere in coding sessions, so `::` and `x::` must not count as IPv6 addresses. ### 1e. `ERR_RESIDUAL`: Claude Code tool schemas (`name:Claude`) ```jsonl {"attachment":{"tools":[{"schema":{"input_schema":{"properties":{"capabilities":{"description":"name:Claude"}}}}},{"schema":{"description":"name:..."}}]}} {"rendered":[{"content":"Claude..."}]} ``` The product name `Claude` (and `...`) becomes a personal seed taken from a tool description. Fails in stream mode; the in-memory `sanitizeJsonl` passes. This is the main reason Claude Code sessions fail (9 of 146 pass). **Expected:** a `name` / `nom` label value must look like a person's name before it is confirmed. That excludes JSON or JS literals (`null`, `true`, `undefined`), punctuation-only values, the label word itself, product names and lowercase identifiers. Propagation and redaction must also act only inside JSON **string values** when `structured` is set, and never on keys, literals or structural characters. ## 2. `ERR_RESIDUAL`: `ENCODED_SENSITIVE` found but never redacted ```jsonl {"toolUseResult":{"stdout":"\"Elon Musk"}} ``` `inspect` reports `ENCODED_SENSITIVE/encoded` (0.85) on `\"Elon Musk`, but redaction leaves it unchanged. Verification finds the same finding again and fails. This is a public figure, so it should probably be preserved. Either way, detection and redaction disagree. ## 3. `ERR_ENCODING` on an escaped cookie header ```jsonl {"payload":{"content":[{"text":"\"cookie:;\\n\""}]}} ``` `SECRET/cookie` matches across the escaped quote and `\\n`, and redaction throws `ERR_ENCODING`. (`sanitizeJsonl` passes; `sanitize`/stream fail.) This blocked 36 Codex sessions with `curl -H "Cookie: ..."` style commands. ## 4. `ERR_FINDING` from `inspect` on an `Authorization:` header ```jsonl {"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01EXAMPLE":{"command":"Authorization:\""}}} {"toolUseResult":{"stderr":""}} ``` `inspect` itself throws `ERR_FINDING`, which suggests an internal finding with an invalid span when the credential label sits at the end of a JSON string. This is the Claude Code `wireToolInputs` record shape. ## 5. `ERR_LATE_PERSONAL` even with `twoPass: true` 10 files still fail with `ERR_LATE_PERSONAL` under `twoPass: true`. Instrumenting `streamIdentity.confirm()` on one of them shows two problems: 1. Pass 1 registers the value with a trailing space: ``` .[0].status,result:.[0].conclusion,count:length})),failures:(.statuscheckrollup|map(select(.conclusion == ``` Pass 2 confirms the same value **without** the trailing space and as a `STATE/known-personal` finding, so `values.has(normalized)` misses and pass 2 throws `ERR_LATE_PERSONAL`. Pass 1 and pass 2 must produce the same seed for the same text, for example by trimming before normalizing, or by matching pass-2 `known-personal` findings against the registry instead of re-seeding from them. 2. The value comes from a public `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup --jq '{...map({state:.[0].status,...})...}'` command. `STATE/catalog/azure` reads the jq object key `state:` as a US-state / location label. This part reproduces synthetically: ```js inspect(JSON.stringify({ text: `gh pr view 1 --json statusCheckRollup --jq '{counts:(.statusCheckRollup|map({state:.[0].status,result:.[0].conclusion,count:length}))}'` }), { profile: 'publication', structured: 'json' }); // → STATE/catalog/azure on ".[0].status,result:.[0].conclusion,count:length}))..." ``` The same run also registered `==` and `check` as personal values. I could not reproduce the pass-1/pass-2 mismatch synthetically in a small file: it needs about 70 records of the real session. The instrumented output above is the evidence. A unit test where pass 2 gets a `known-personal` finding whose span differs from the registered value only in surrounding whitespace should cover it. **Expected:** under `twoPass: true`, pass 2 must never throw `ERR_LATE_PERSONAL`, because every value is known after pass 1. If pass 2 still finds something new, it should redact it, not fail. ## 6. Leak (minor): `tel:` links without `+` and `Fax:` labels are not detected This one was found by an independent audit of the 418 **passing** outputs. A fetched public organization web page kept its phone numbers, while the email on the same page was redacted: ```js sanitize(JSON.stringify({ text: 'Fax: 028 12 345 678' }), { profile: 'publication', structured: 'json' }) // unchanged sanitize(JSON.stringify({ text: 'ĐT' }), ...) // unchanged sanitize(JSON.stringify({ text: 'tel:+84812345678' }), ...) // tel:[REDACTED] (OK) sanitize(JSON.stringify({ text: 'Phone: 028 12 345 678' }), ...) // Phone: [REDACTED] (OK) ``` **Expected:** a `tel:` URI is always a phone number (with or without `+`), and `Fax:` / `ĐT` (Vietnamese "điện thoại") should be phone labels. The rest of the audit found no MRZ, passport, SNILS, INN, PNR, DOB, email, card, token or home-path leaks in the passing outputs. ## Acceptance - The reproductions in 1–4 and 6 publish with valid JSON and zero residual findings, keep `null` / keys / structure untouched, and keep code tokens (`codec::`, `nom::{`, `Claude`). - `twoPass: true` never throws `ERR_LATE_PERSONAL`. - Add Codex `turn_context` / `rate_limits` records and Claude Code `attachment.tools` / `wireToolInputs` / `toolUseResult` record shapes to the CI publication corpus from #35. Related: #34, #35. npm publication remains tracked in #28 (package is still 404 on npm).

title: fix: unblock session publication with bounded detection and two-pass redaction
body:
Closes #34.

Escaped newlines let an `Organization:` or `phone` label swallow an entire JSON string and feed that value into propagation. The bounded reproduction changed a 30,440-character source record to 60 characters; it now preserves the complete source. The complete reported public CI record also publishes without residual findings.

- Bound personal label values at raw/escaped delimiters (512 UTF-16 units), require phone/email shapes, bound inferred propagation seeds to 256 units, build patterns safely, and wrap unexpected internal exceptions in typed failures.
- Require a real filename/path and plausible name words for document names. Preserve ordinary JSON identifier keys during detection and after propagation; explicitly known private keys and credentials still redact. Preserve the six reported CI service accounts and fix the `passes` credential-label false positive.
- Add `twoPass: true` to atomic file APIs and `--stream --two-pass` to the CLI. Discovery snapshots one-shot input privately and collects identities; redaction uses the complete registry in ordered workers. Limits, required detectors, residual verification, target preservation, and spool cleanup remain active. One-pass streaming keeps its existing default behavior.
- Preserve valid escaped lone surrogates alongside emoji and redactions. Malformed UTF-8 remains blocked with JSONL record and byte offsets, including across the bounded worker and CLI.
- Add a CI publication corpus with Codex/Claude record shapes, complete public Codex and Guardian prompts with upstream attribution/license, Claude Code excerpts, a 937-line source output, the entire reported CI output, identifiers, late confirmations, and Unicode. It runs with one/four workers and requires preserved content, zero failures, and zero residual findings.

Reproduce and verify:

```sh
node --max-old-space-size=512 --stack-size=4096 experiments/issue-34/reproduce.mjs
node --test tests/sanitizer-issue-34.test.js tests/sanitizer-two-pass.test.js
node --max-old-space-size=512 experiments/issue-34/session-corpus.mjs
```

Validation completed locally:

- Full Node suite: 1,250 passing tests; focused stream checks after the final error-handling change: 26 passing tests.
- Full Bun suite: 1,251 passing tests. Full Deno suite: 1,106 passing tests and 8 steps, zero failures.
- Focused structured/name checks after the helper refactor; workflow policy tests; lint, formatting, duplication, secrets, syntax, file-size, documentation and release guards.
- Four corpus publications (two sessions × one/four workers), all with zero residual findings. A minor Changeset prepares the automatic release; package versions are unchanged as required by repository policy.

Hosted CI also passes on commit `8711709`: Node, Bun, and Deno on Linux, macOS, and Windows; all repository checks; security and example-app workflows. The [session publication job](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/38219986885/job/114713683175) publishes all four corpus combinations with zero residual findings.

The [case study](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-34-979b472b0be1/docs/case-studies/issue-34/README.md) records root causes, baseline evidence, tests and limits. The private session files were not supplied; the public corpus does not contain the complete Claude Code system prompt. The bounded probes reproduce swallowed text; the reported raw stack overflow depends on the runtime's regex compiler, and oversized-seed tests verify it cannot be reached through propagation. Two-pass mode needs disk space for raw input and sanitized output. Corpus timings are reported without claiming a large-session throughput guarantee. npm owner setup remains tracked separately in #28.

title: Real sessions still blocked after #33: label spans across escaped JSON newlines crash propagation, JSON keys read as names, CI paths as users
body:
## Summary

Re-verification after #33 (main @ c60b9e1) with `profile: publication` and `structured: jsonl`. The probes and minimal reproductions from #18 to #31 now pass: 34/34 identity probes, bare passport, SNILS and INN masked, `userName = getUserName()` untouched, and the #30 snippets stay valid JSON. However, real sessions still cannot be published:

- documents-processing (13 files): 12 fail (`ERR_RESIDUAL`, `ERR_OUTPUT`, `ERR_JSON_COLLISION`).
- public repositories, all session files up to 5 MB, partial run: of the first 62, 40 crash with `SyntaxError`, 2 fail with `ERR_ENCODING`, and 20 pass.
- a 23 MB public Codex session: `ERR_RESIDUAL` with `workers: 1`, `ERR_LATE_PERSONAL` with `workers: 4`.

The library fails closed, so nothing leaks, but almost nothing can be published.

## 1. Label value spans the rest of a JSON string, then propagation crashes (`SyntaxError: Stack overflow`)

Inside a JSON string, line breaks are escaped `\n`. A `phone`/`email` label value therefore runs to the end of the string, up to a whole 937-line file. Propagation then compiles that value into a RegExp. The error is not an `ERR_*` failure: streaming reports it as `ERR_OUTPUT` and `sanitizeJsonl` throws a raw `SyntaxError`.

```js
const s = createSanitizer({ profile: 'publication' });
const body = (n) => Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => `  const value${i} = compute(${i});`).join('
');
const src = (n) => `function parse(line, found, number) {
  if (relation) {
    found.emergencyRelationship ??= relation;
  } else {
    found.phone = number;
  }
${body(n)}
}`;
await s.sanitize(src(5));                                   // "found.phone = [REDACTED]"  (code identifier as a phone)
await s.sanitize(JSON.stringify({ content: src(5) }));      // 314 chars -> 24 chars: whole file content replaced (PHONE:label 165 chars)
await s.sanitize(JSON.stringify({ content: src(900) }));    // throws SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression ... Stack overflow
```

Expected: label values stop at escaped line breaks and quotes, and have a bounded length. A phone or email value must look like one, not like code (`number;`). Propagation escapes and bounds seeds, never compiles values above a small limit, and turns every internal exception into an `ERR_*` failure.

## 2. JSON keys are treated as names (regression from #26), then key collisions block records

```js
const p = createSanitizer({ profile: 'publication' });
await p.sanitize('root_turn_id');                          // "[REDACTED]_id"  PERSON:name-document
const j = createSanitizer({ structured: 'jsonl', profile: 'publication' });
await j.sanitizeJsonl('{"payload":{"root_turn_id":"x","other_turn_id":"y"}}
'); // ERR_JSON_COLLISION
```

Codex session records contain `turn_id` and `root_turn_id`. Expected: the document-file-name rule requires a real file name (an extension or a path) and gazetteer or name-shaped words, not `snake_case` identifiers. Structured mode never rewrites JSON keys that are ordinary identifiers.

## 3. CI logs: GitHub Actions paths treated as personal

```text
node:internal/test_runner/test:835:12             -> node:internal/test_[REDACTED]/test:835:12
location: '/home/runner/work/example-repo/...'   -> location: '[REDACTED]'
# Subtest: passes the standalone validator used by the filing workflow -> passes [REDACTED]
/home/runner/work/_temp/...   /github/runner_temp/... -> /home/[REDACTED]/...  /github/[REDACTED]_temp/...
```

`runner` (and `ubuntu`, `vsts`, `circleci`, `node`, `root`) are well-known service accounts, not personal user names. Propagating them into `test_runner` and `runner_temp` is wrong.

The same public CI output also triggers `ERR_RESIDUAL` in structured mode. Line-level minimisation does not shrink it, because the failure needs the propagation state built by several lines. The record below is public GitHub Actions output from link-foundation/relative-meta-logic.
