title: fix: protect session publication across batches and JSON encodings
body:
Confirmed personal identities now follow large sessions across JSONL batches and
Cyrillic/passport spellings. Valid session JSON remains valid after redaction,
and CLI publication protects bare identity numbers through a documented profile.
This single PR addresses the complete #32 scope, with the external npm publication
prerequisite described explicitly below.

For example, `SIDOROV_ALEKSEI_PHOTO.png` now produces a structural PERSON finding;
an MRZ in the first stream batch protects later `zyryanova.pdf`; and the reported
`state:\nt` session record survives unchanged. `profile: 'publication'` selects
a 0.3 personal threshold and identity masking, while explicit options retain
their precedence.

## Scope and implementation

- #26: bounded two/three-token document filename grammar, Slavic prose pairs in
  either order, systematic transliteration aliases, and a private per-stream
  confirmation registry shared with ordered workers. HMAC token history detects
  late confirmation and blocks completed publication; limits and isolation are tested.
- #27 and #31: restore distinctive formatted SNILS and personal 12-digit INN
  scoring, extend Russian SNILS/English passport context, and add the publication
  profile to APIs, declarations, CLI and documentation. Bare organizational INN
  remains low confidence; timestamp/order exclusions remain covered.
- #29 and #31: independently sourced public figures, private-namesake and credential
  precedence, booking/status/place/code negatives, and type-preserving fictional
  phone ranges. Existing deterministic fake MRZ/date/name/ID behavior remains covered.
- #30: shared same-line label plausibility and complete JSON escape boundaries
  across native/async/structured rendering. Recursive encoded strings carry
  document confirmations without promoting encoding wrappers to identities.
  The document-label guard also removes a CodeQL-confirmed quadratic whitespace
  ambiguity with a bounded before/after regression. Serial streams reuse prepared findings; workers reuse coordinator native results.
  Required engines still inspect input and final output.
- #28: disabled/legacy Pages skips deployment while retaining the web build artifact;
  permission/server failures remain visible. The alleged Bun Windows crash was
  identified in full logs as a hostile-whitespace test deadline failure. Readiness
  now separates child startup/imports from the original bounded matching deadline;
  no retries or relaxed regex-time assertion are used.

[Every requirement, alternatives, selected plans and primary-source component research](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-32-18721f994a02/docs/case-studies/issue-32/REQUIREMENTS.md),
[reproduction and validation evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-32-18721f994a02/docs/case-studies/issue-32/VALIDATION.md),
and [all seven issue descriptions and paginated comments](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/tree/issue-32-18721f994a02/docs/case-studies/issue-32/data)
are committed for review. No previously delivered detector, required engine or
publication verification is removed.

## Reproduction and validation

Regression tests first reproduced the reported filename/name leaks, national-ID
scores, public/code/place false positives, JSON escape failures and cross-batch
propagation gaps. Further finite experiments reproduced lost confirmations in
encoded credential-containing strings and late-confirmation gaps in compound
usernames/addresses. Automated regressions cover these cases, supplied sanitizers,
registry isolation/exhaustion, private public-figure namesakes and atomic file cleanup.

The original private 13-session corpus was unavailable. Tests use both exact
minimal reproductions and synthetic Claude/Codex-shaped nested records with diffs
and test output, including worker counts 1/4 and a 1.7 MB distant-MRZ session.
Performance results and complete local/runtime commands are in VALIDATION.md.
The existing 7 MiB parallel-record and 10 MiB publication tests retain 30-second
deadlines. One minor Changeset prepares the next version; package.json is unchanged.

- Complete local suites: Node 1,208 passed; Bun 1,208 passed; Deno 1,063
  passed plus 8 steps. The final helper extraction additionally passes all 92
  focused session/escape/stream cases on all three runtimes.
- `npm run check`, zero-warning changed-file ESLint, secret scan, syntax,
  file-size, documentation, workflow policy, version and Changeset guards pass.
- Fresh packed install: API, installed CLI and version consistency pass at
  0.11.31; the installed offline npm launcher and both session examples pass.
- Finite 2,191,272-byte session: whole JSONL 2.793 s, serial stream 2.069 s,
  four-worker stream 2.500 s. All 26 records parse and private values are removed.

## npm publication and main CI prerequisite

First public npm publication is **still externally blocked**: fresh registry
lookup returns E404, repository secret-name listing is empty, and local npm
authentication returns ENEEDAUTH. A packed install verifies API and installed CLI
contents independently of this checkout; it does not establish a public release.

The existing release workflow already supports bootstrap credentials and subsequent
OIDC. An npm owner must create the scoped package using an authorized bootstrap
publish or the newly supported staged first publish with owner approval, then
configure trusted publishing for `link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer` and
workflow **release.yml**. Current new publisher configurations default to staged
publishing, so permit direct publishing when retaining this workflow's behavior.
[Exact owner steps and supported Node/npm prerequisites](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-32-18721f994a02/docs/case-studies/issue-32/REQUIREMENTS.md#exact-npm-owner-steps)

title: Re-verification of #15-#23: default minConfidence publishes bare passport/SNILS/INN, npm still unpublished, code over-redaction
body:
## Summary

A re-verification of #15 to #23 after #25 found items that were closed without being delivered, plus default behaviour that is unsafe for publication.

## 1. The default `minConfidence: 0.5` publishes bare identity numbers (regression for publication use)

These were redacted at 2306fda. Now they are detected (the findings are present) but not replaced:

```js
const s = createSanitizer();
await s.sanitize('46 21 573918');                      // PASSPORT_NUMBER:passport-format, not replaced
await s.sanitize('4621 573918');                       // not replaced
await s.sanitize('series and number: 46 21 573918');   // English label does not raise confidence ("серия и номер:" does)
await s.sanitize('487-192-053 19');                    // RU_SNILS with valid checksum, not replaced
await s.sanitize('771829456048');                      // RU_INN with valid checksum, not replaced
```

`minConfidence: 0.3` fixes all of them while keeping the #15 timestamps and order ids untouched. Please:

- add a documented publication profile, for example `profile: 'publication'`, with `minConfidence: 0.3`, `identityMask` and the other strict defaults, and make the CLI `redact` used for publishing default to it;
- treat English `series and number`, `passport series`, `document number` like the Russian labels.

## 2. #23 closed but the package is still not on npm

`npm view @link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer` returns 404, and `package.json` is still 0.11.31.

## 3. Over-redaction of ordinary code

```js
await s.sanitize('const userName = getUserName();');   // => "const userName = [REDACTED]"  (USERNAME:label)
```

A label followed by a function call, an identifier or a property access is code, not a username.

## Verified as delivered

MRZ (including truncated and OCR-damaged lines), passport labels, booking references (bare `booking`, file names, paths), names in file names, Russian full names and Latin prose, MRZ-to-prose propagation, `identityMask` spans, `fakeValues`, ID/TH phones, #15 timestamps and order ids, #16 git and HTTP headers, and `mode: 'fake'`. The fake mode produces valid MRZ check digits, valid dates, script-preserving names consistent between the MRZ and prose, deterministic output, and redacted credentials.

title: Regression after #25: structured JSONL fails with ERR_JSON/ERR_RESIDUAL on 9 of 13 real sessions; plain mode splits JSON escapes
Over-redaction: inconsistent public figures, uppercase words as booking refs, implausible fake phones
body:
## Summary

These are over-redaction and quality problems found while re-checking #15–#23 on main @ c9714cb. None of them leak data, but they damage published sessions and conflict with #1 (public people should not be treated as personal data) and #5 (ordinary uppercase words after "booking" are negatives).

### 1. Public figures handled inconsistently

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `Linus Torvalds`, `Elon Musk tweeted`, `Bill Gates`, `Nelson Mandela`, `Satya Nadella`, `Tim Cook`, `Grace Hopper` | kept |
| `Sergey Brin founded Google` | `[REDACTED] founded Google` |
| `Pavel Durov said` | `[REDACTED] said` |
| `Vladimir Putin` | `[REDACTED]` |

The result appears to depend on whether the first name is in the (Slavic) gazetteer, not on whether the person is public. Expected: the bundled public-entity catalog (or `createWikidataVerifier`) takes precedence over the gazetteer for well-known public figures regardless of the name's origin. Add these as fixtures.

### 2. Uppercase words and places taken as identifiers or names

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `Booking FAILED today` | `Booking [REDACTED] today` (`BOOKING_REFERENCE`) |
| `reservation HTTP 500` | `reservation [REDACTED] 500` |
| `Marina Bay Sands hotel` | `[REDACTED] Sands hotel` (`PERSON`) |

Expected: booking references must contain at least one digit or match a PNR shape that is not a dictionary word. Add negatives for common uppercase log words (`FAILED`, `ERROR`, `HTTP`, `PENDING`, `OK`, `CANCELLED`, `CONFIRMED`). A first name directly followed by a known place/brand word (`Bay`, `Sands`, `Hotel`, `Street`) should not become a person on its own.

### 3. Fake mode: phones not in a plausible or reserved range (#22)

`mode: 'fake'` turns `phone +7 912 555-01-42` into `+7 227 479-47-38`. The country code and length are kept, but `227` is not a Russian mobile range, and #22 asked to prefer reserved fictional ranges where available. Expected: keep the number type (mobile stays `9xx` for RU) and use reserved/fictional ranges where they exist (NANP 555-01xx, Ofcom drama ranges, …).

The faked MRZ, dates, SNILS, names and emails were verified to be valid, deterministic per key and different across keys. Credentials stay fully redacted.

title: Regression from #15: bare formatted SNILS and 12-digit INN no longer redacted (required by #11)
body:
## Summary

The fix for #15 (bare checksum matches get confidence 0.35 and are not replaced under the default `minConfidence: 0.5`) also turned off detection that #11 explicitly required. #11: "Russian SNILS (`ddd-ddd-ddd dd` with checksum) and INN (10/12 digits with checksum) without labels. With a `snils`/`inn` label both are detected; bare values such as `112-233-445 95` are not."

On main @ c9714cb:

| Input (synthetic, checksum-valid) | Result |
|---|---|
| `СНИЛС 112-233-445 95`, `snils 11223344595` | redacted ✅ |
| `112-233-445 95` | **unchanged** (`RU_SNILS` 0.35) |
| `пенсионное 112-233-445 95` (common Russian name of SNILS) | **unchanged** (0.35) |
| `value 500100732259` (12-digit personal INN) | **unchanged** (`RU_INN` 0.35) |

Plain 10-digit numbers matching INN/NHS/NPI checksums by chance are a different case from the SNILS shape. `ddd-ddd-ddd dd` with exactly that punctuation and a valid checksum almost never appears by accident in logs: it is strong structural evidence on its own, like a formatted credit card number. A 12-digit INN with two check digits passes by chance only about 1 in 100 times, unlike the 1-in-10 10-digit INN.

## Expected

- SNILS in its formatted shape `ddd-ddd-ddd dd` (and `ddd ddd ddd dd`) with a valid checksum scores ≥ 0.85 without context.
- 12-digit INN (two check digits) scores above the default threshold, or at least above it whenever any Russian-language text is in the same record. 10-digit INN stays low without context, as #15 requires.
- Add SNILS context words: `пенсионное`, `страховое свидетельство`, `СНИЛС`, `страховой номер`.
- Add a test asserting the confidence for each national-ID shape, so a future threshold change cannot silently disable a required detector. List the effective default behaviour per ID type in COVERAGE.md.

title: Names still leak after #20: file names with non-gazetteer names, Slavic name pairs in prose, propagation across stream batches
body:
## Summary

#20 is closed, but personal names still leak in the same forms that caused the original incident. Detection depends on the first name being in the gazetteer. Names next to document words in file names are found only when both parts are known gazetteer entries. Document-level propagation does not cross streaming batches, which is the only way to process the large sessions where the leak happened.

All values below are synthetic. Tested on main @ c9714cb with `createSanitizer({})`.

### 1. File names with document words (explicitly required by #20)

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `KOVALEVA_MARINA_PASSPORT.jpg`, `IVANOV_IVAN_SCAN.pdf`, `KUZNETSOVA-EKATERINA-ID.png` | redacted ✅ |
| `SIDOROV_ALEKSEI_PHOTO.png` | **unchanged** |
| `SIDOROV-ALEKSEI-PHOTO.png` | **unchanged** |
| `TKACHENKO_BOGDAN_VISA.pdf` | **unchanged** |
| `ZHANG_WEI_PASSPORT.pdf` | **unchanged** (`Zhang Wei` in prose *is* redacted) |
| `NGUYEN_VAN_AN_PASSPORT.jpg` | **unchanged** |
| `scan_passport_kovaleva_marina.jpg` (lowercase, document word first) | **unchanged** |
| `ПАСПОРТ_Ковалева_Марина.pdf` (Cyrillic; `ПАСПОРТ` is listed in #20) | **unchanged** |

Expected: two or three name-shaped tokens joined by `_`/`-` next to a document word (PASSPORT, VISA, ID, PHOTO, SCAN, ПАСПОРТ, ВИЗА, СКАН, ФОТО), in either order and any case, are `PERSON` structurally. A gazetteer hit should only raise confidence, not be required.

### 2. Name pairs in prose (required by #20: "transliterated Slavic surnames -ova, -eva, -ov, -ev, -in, -ina, -enko, -sky")

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `Alexey Sidorov`, `Ekaterina Kuznetsova` | redacted ✅ |
| `for Olesya Zyryanova`, `Zyryanova Olesya` | **unchanged** |
| `Aleksei Sidorov` (common transliteration of the same name) | **unchanged** |
| `Bogdan Tkachenko` | **unchanged** |
| `Ковалева Марина`, `Зырянова Олеся` (Cyrillic, no patronymic, no label) | **unchanged** |

Expected: a capitalised (or all-caps) given-name-shaped token adjacent to a token with a Slavic surname suffix counts as a name pair. Transliteration variants of gazetteer names (`Aleksei/Alexei/Alexey/Aleksey`, `Olesya/Olesia`) must be covered systematically, for example through transliteration normalisation of the gazetteer instead of single spellings. Cyrillic surname-suffix + first-name pairs need the same rule.

### 3. Propagation stops at streaming batch boundaries

`sanitizeStream(src, {structured: 'jsonl'})` on a 1.7 MB JSONL: the first record holds a synthetic MRZ for `ZYRYANOVA<<OLESYA`, and the last record says `saved zyryanova_olesya_scan.png for Olesya Zyryanova`. **The last record is published unchanged.** The same text through `sanitize()` (one batch) is redacted. API.md documents "Document propagation is within a scanned batch", but streaming exists precisely for the large sessions where this leak happened (#23). Propagation also does not cross scripts: `ФИО: Зырянова Олеся` + `файл zyryanova.pdf` redacts only the Cyrillic name.

Expected:
- The stream keeps a bounded, private per-stream registry of confirmed personal values (from MRZ, labelled fields and strong rules) and applies it to all later batches. Because earlier batches are already emitted, a confirmed value seen only *after* its first occurrence must either be handled by a two-pass mode (`sanitizeStreamToFile` can scan twice) or make the stream fail closed.
- Confirmed Cyrillic names propagate in their standard transliterations (ICAO 9303 / GOST 7.79 / common passport spellings) and back.

### Tests

Add every input above as a regression fixture, plus a stream test where the confirmation and the reuse are more than one batch apart.

title: feat: Improve session accuracy, realistic fakes and JSONL throughput
body:
Ordinary session metadata now survives sanitization, while confirmed personal identities and credentials are protected across plain text, encoded views, structured fields, paths and residual verification. This single PR addresses the complete umbrella scope in #24.

For example, `ts=1696110866` remains intact; `passport no AB1234XYZ` masks the value as `passport no AB***YZ`; confirmed booking/name values are also removed from filenames. Opt-in keyed fake mode produces realistic supported names, dates, MRZs and checksummed IDs, with credentials fully redacted by default. Large JSONL sessions use ordered, byte-bounded record workers without disabling the default scanners.

## Scope and implementation

- #15–#16: shared personal confidence threshold (default 0.5), contextual checksum scores, epoch/metadata negatives, card IIN/length validation, auth key boundaries and personal-only date detection.
- #17–#18 and #21: per-document specimen policy, narrow German specimen fragments, precise identity/assignment spans, ID/TH/VN phones, digit-bearing visa identifiers, consistent escaped projection and reviewed fake-value matching. Contextual four-character identities receive full redaction.
- #19–#20: contextual and filename booking/name recognizers plus confirmed-value propagation across whole-document fields and paths, including reordered unknown labelled names.
- #22: deterministic HMAC-seeded locale generators, shared calendar shifts with century transitions, independently valid MRZs, national/card/IBAN arithmetic, reserved contact destinations, explicit invalid FAKE credential opt-in and private generated-value provenance. Documentation describes pseudonymisation and format/inference limits.

Deno uses the in-process fallback; Bun ignores worker resourceLimits, which is documented.

[Every requirement, alternatives, selected solution plans and primary-source library research](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-24-4efef94003ab/docs/case-studies/issue-24/REQUIREMENTS.md), [reproduction/root-cause evidence and resource limits](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-24-4efef94003ab/docs/case-studies/issue-24/README.md), and [all issue bodies/comments](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-24-4efef94003ab/docs/case-studies/issue-24/issues.json) are committed for review. Existing transformations, public policy, required scanners and fail-closed publication remain covered.

Additional failing regressions demonstrated patient-context confidence, wrapped MRZ names, inherited eval/V8 worker flags, century transitions and adjacent real identities beside a German specimen. Final diff review reproduced card leaks under support/report/runtime labels, a false positive on a future epoch that passed Visa/Luhn, and invalid card fakes through catalog aliases. Unicode boundaries, contextual epoch handling and canonical alias generation now cover these cases. These are now automated regression tests.

- Complete sequential suites passed: Node 1,112/1,112, Bun 1,112/1,112, Deno 967/967 plus eight steps.

title: Large session throughput (0.12 MB/s) and npm release of the merged identity work
body:
## Summary

Sessions large enough to need sanitizing are often very large. In the original publication, sessions of 70 MB to 760 MB had to be skipped.

Measured on main @ 2306fda with `structured: 'jsonl'`:

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 5 MB Codex session | about 40 s (about 0.12 MB/s) |
| 157 MB Claude session | `ERR_LIMIT` with `sanitizeJsonl()`, because the whole text must fit under `maxInputLength` |

## Expected

- `sanitizeStream(source, { structured: 'jsonl' })` already works on small inputs. Document it next to `sanitizeJsonl()` as the way to process files above `maxInputLength`, and test it with records up to about 7 MB, since single session records reach that size.
- Throughput of about 1 MB/s or better on session JSONL, using worker parallelism over records with deterministic output order. Today a 760 MB session takes hours.

title: Sanitization by faking: realistic same-format fake values (valid MRZ, dates, checksums, script-preserving names)
body:
## Summary

Add sanitization by faking: replace real values with realistic fake values of the same format, so published sessions stay readable and their code paths, tests and parsers still work. Today `format-preserving` produces character-class noise, and `pseudonym` produces opaque tags.

## Current behaviour (main @ 2306fda, synthetic input)

```text
format-preserving:
  P<RUSKOVALEVA<<MARINA<<<…  ->  Z<ZCRCEXHADTT<<ZDQAAR<<<…   (invalid document code, invalid state, letters only)
  5839204716RUS8204117M310519<<…  ->  7936874368RTY3267065H912481<<…  (invalid country RTY, sex H, impossible dates, wrong check digits)
  Ковалева Марина Сергеевна  ->  qprwhpqc geasxb jzdxreurb   (Cyrillic replaced with Latin noise)
  born on 07/12/1985  ->  born on 55/46/5121                 (impossible date)
  phone +7 912 555-01-42  ->  +5 585 882-10-71               (country code changed)
pseudonym:
  every value -> [PSEUDONYM_2856bd99eef0eebb9ecf79d4]
credentials: always [REDACTED] (no fake option)
```

## Proposal: `mode: 'fake'`

Keyed and deterministic, so the same input value always maps to the same fake within a run, and consistently across types:

- **Names:** fake names from the same locale and script and gender (Cyrillic stays Cyrillic, patronymic stays a patronymic). The same person is consistent between the MRZ, prose, labelled fields and file names.
- **Dates:** valid calendar dates, shifted by a keyed offset, with the original format kept (`dd/mm/yyyy`, ISO, `dd.mm.yyyy`). Birth dates stay plausible, for example adults stay adults.
- **Passport MRZ:** valid ICAO 9303 lines with real check digits. The issuing state and nationality are kept, or replaced by `UTO` (configurable). Name fields match the faked name, and date fields match the faked birth and expiry dates.
- **Document numbers and national IDs:** same length and pattern with valid checksums (SNILS, INN, PESEL, Luhn and others). Prefer reserved or specimen ranges where they exist.
- **Phones:** keep the country code and number length. Use reserved fictional ranges where available, such as NANP 555-01xx and Ofcom drama numbers.
- **Emails and domains:** fake local parts on reserved domains (`example.com`, `.test`).
- **Credentials (opt-in):** a provider-shaped fake that cannot be valid and carries a visible marker, for example `ghp_FAKE…`. It must not trip GitHub push protection or other scanners, and full redaction stays the default for credentials.
- Every fake is recognisable by the residual verifier (`kept: 'fake'` / `faked: true` findings), so verification does not loop on its own output. The `fakeIdentity` policy also recognises fakes produced by this mode.
- Document that faked output is a pseudonymisation, not anonymisation: the key must stay private, and structure such as dates and relations is partly preserved.

## Tests

Round-trip properties: generated MRZ lines pass check-digit validation. Dates parse. Checksummed IDs validate. Scripts are preserved. The same input maps to the same output under one key and to different output under another key. No original value survives.

title: identityMask/fakeValues: label findings include label words ("no***YZ") and ignore allowlisted values
body:
## Summary

With `identityMask: true`, a generic `ID:label` finding claims a span that includes the label words, so the mask shows label text instead of the value. `fakeValues` is ignored for the same reason.

## Reproduction

```js
const s = createSanitizer({ identityMask: true, fakeValues: ['AB1234XYZ'] });
await s.sanitize('passport no AB1234XYZ');      // => "passport no***YZ"   (expected "passport no AB1234XYZ", allowlisted)
await s.sanitize('passport number: AB1234XYZ'); // => "passport nu***YZ"   (label text leaks into the mask)
await s.sanitize('passport no 7549302813');     // => "passport no***13"   (expected "passport no 75***13")
// findings: ID:label spans start at "no" / "number: ", not at the value
```

## Expected

- Label findings start at the value, not at trailing label words like `no`, `no.`, `number:`, `#` or `№`.
- Passport context produces `PASSPORT_NUMBER`, not the generic `ID`, so identity policies apply uniformly.
- `fakeValues` matching uses the value span, and also a whole token when a detector span is a substring of it.
- Short values: `pnr: AB12` is not detected at all. Decide whether 4-character values after booking or passport context should be fully redacted, as the identity policy suggests.

title: Personal names leak in document file names, Russian full names and Latin prose
body:
## Summary

Personal names still pass in the forms in which a family's names leaked. The leak happened through document file names and applicant prose. Passport MRZ lines are now redacted, but the same names elsewhere are not.

## Reproduction (synthetic names)

```js
const s = createSanitizer();
for (const t of [
  'KOVALEVA-MARINA-PASSPORT.jpg and PETROV-IVAN-VISA.pdf',
  'Заявитель: Ковалева Марина Сергеевна, 1985 г.р.',
  'Marina Kovaleva and marina kovaleva again',
]) console.log((await s.sanitize(t)).text);
// All three are returned unchanged.
```

## Expected

- Upper-case and hyphen- or underscore-joined name pairs in file names next to document words (PASSPORT, VISA, ID, PHOTO, SCAN, ПАСПОРТ), using the name gazetteer in transliterated form.
- Russian full names with a patronymic (`-вич`, `-вна`, `-ична`, `оглы`, `кызы`) as a strong signal on their own. Labels like Заявитель, ФИО, Applicant, Passenger, Traveller as context.
- Common Latin first-name + surname pairs in prose, case-insensitively, including transliterated Slavic surnames (`-ova`, `-eva`, `-ov`, `-ev`, `-in`, `-ina`, `-enko`, `-sky`).
- Document-level propagation: a name confirmed in an MRZ or a labelled field is redacted at every other occurrence in the same input. In the leak, MRZ names reappeared in file names and messages.

title: Booking references still leak after bare "booking", in file names and path segments
body:
## Summary

Booking references still leak in the forms they actually take in sessions. A real session kept a real booking reference 23 times after #14.

## Reproduction (synthetic values)

```js
const s = createSanitizer();
for (const t of [
  "This trip's affected flights are on Air India booking K7QWZP",
  "out: 'AirIndia-K7QWZP-2-AI0000-AAA-BBB-cancelled.pdf'",
  "const SUPPORT_DIR = path.join(FINAL, 'K7QWZP');",
]) console.log((await s.sanitize(t)).text);
// K7QWZP survives in all three
```

## Expected

- `booking`, `reservation`, `PNR`, `confirmation` and `бронь` alone, followed by a 5–8 character uppercase alphanumeric token, count as booking context. This includes airline names in between ("Air India booking K7QWZP").
- A value confirmed as a booking reference anywhere in the same input is redacted at every occurrence, including inside file names and path segments. This is a document-level propagation of confirmed values, which would also help passport numbers and names.
- Airline-prefixed file names `<Airline>-<PNR>-...` count as booking context.

title: ERR_RESIDUAL blocks real sessions and the visa rule redacts words without digits
body:
## Summary

After #14, real AI session files are blocked with `ERR_RESIDUAL`. It fails closed, which is safe, but those sessions can never be published. The minimal reproduction contains no personal data. A second bug shows up alongside it: the new visa rule redacts ordinary words that contain no digits.

## Reproduction (main @ 2306fda)

```js
const s = createSanitizer();
await s.sanitize('{"stdout":"nameis\\nvisawindo"}');   // throws ERR_RESIDUAL
await s.sanitize('name is\nvisa window');              // => "name is\nvisa [REDACTED]"
await s.sanitize('nameis visawindo');                  // => "nameis [REDACTED]"
```

The same happens with `structured: 'jsonl'` + `sanitizeJsonl()`. Two of the ten Codex session files tested (about 5 MB each) failed this way. The trigger was ordinary code-review prose containing the word "visa" in an escaped JSON string.

## Expected

- `VISA_NUMBER` requires at least one digit, and a shape of an actual visa or e-visa identifier, not any word after "visa".
- The escaped-JSON projection and the residual verification agree on spans, so no `ERR_RESIDUAL` occurs when the first pass already redacted everything the second pass sees.
- Regression tests: the snippets above, plus prose like "the visa window closes", "visa application form", "Visa card".

title: Remaining gaps from #8 and #12: MRZ fake check per document, ID/TH phone formats, label words in identity spans
body:
## Summary

Two acceptance cases from #8 and #12 still fail on main @ 2306fda. A third (span precision) is minor.

### 1. Fake identity: descending document number is redacted when the MRZ name line is present (#8)

With `fakeIdentity: 'specimen-and-synthetic'`:

| Input (synthetic) | Result |
|---|---|
| `9876543217RUS9001014F300101<<<<<<<<<<<<<<04` alone | kept, 2 findings `kept: 'fake'` ✅ |
| `P<RUSTESTOVA<<OLGA<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<` + `\n` + the same line | **whole MRZ `[REDACTED]`, 0 kept** ❌ |
| German specimen `Reisepass C01X00T47 MUSTERMANN ERIKA SPECIMEN` | **`Reisepass [REDACTED]`** ❌ (#8 lists `MUSTERMANN`/`SPECIMEN` as national specimen markers; `C01X00T47` is the published German specimen number) |
| ICAO TD1/TD3 `UTO`/`ERIKSSON` specimens | kept ✅ |

Expected: the fake decision is made per document (the MRZ as a unit, using its document-number field) and applies to all lines of that MRZ. Add the specimen document numbers of common national documents (DE `C01X00T47` / `T22000129`, etc.) and recognize `MUSTERMANN`/`ОБРАЗЕЦ`/`SPECIMEN` when they are part of the same document record. Context words like "test" must still not exempt anything.

### 2. National trunk formats for Indonesia/Thailand only work after messenger labels (#12)

| Input (synthetic) | Result |
|---|---|
| `WhatsApp: 0812 3456 7890` | redacted ✅ |
| `0812 3456 7890` | unchanged ❌ |
| `telp 0812-3456-7890` (Indonesian "phone") | unchanged ❌ |
| `HP: 0812 3456 7890` (Indonesian "mobile") | unchanged ❌ |
| `โทร 08 123 4567` (Thai "call") | unchanged ❌ |
| `gọi 090 123 4567` (Vietnamese "call") | redacted, but as `UK_NHS` (wrong type) |

#12 asked for these trunk formats as format rules, plus local call-to-action context. Expected: add local phone/call vocabulary for at least the languages in #12 (`telp`, `telepon`, `HP`, `hubungi`, `โทร`, `เบอร์`, `gọi`, `SĐT`, `điện thoại`) and the trunk-prefix shapes (with space, dash and parentheses), typed `PHONE`.

### 3. Minor: label words are swallowed into identity spans

`passport no J8369854`, `passport number J8369854`, `passport No. J8369854` all become `passport [REDACTED]`. With `identityMask: true`, `passport no J8369854` becomes `passport no***54`: the kept "first two characters" are the label word `no`, not the value. Expected `passport no J8***54` (#7's 2+2 rule applies to the value). The `ID:label` span should start after `no`/`number`/`No.`/`№`/`#`.

Similarly, prose password context now runs to the end of the line. `password=hunter2 email john@private.org then more text` becomes `password=[REDACTED]`, which hides the unrelated rest of the line. That is safe but over-broad. For `key=value` syntax, the value should stop at whitespace, while prose forms (`password is …`) keep the wider span.

title: 'author' matches as credential label and 'Date:' headers are redacted (git log, HTTP, email)
body:
## Summary

Two context rules fire on very common log fields that are not sensitive:

1. **`author` is treated as a credential label.** The `auth` key affix matches `author`, `authored_by` and `"author":`. Every `git log`/`git show` output, `package.json`, and commit metadata in an AI session gets `SECRET:context` (0.95 VERY_LIKELY).
2. **`Date:` headers are redacted as `DATE` (`catalog/azure` rule).** Git log dates, HTTP `Date:` response headers and email headers are removed. #6 explicitly required: "Keep plain dates (commit dates, timestamps) untouched without birth context."

## Reproduction (main @ 2306fda, `createSanitizer({})`)

| Input | Output | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| `author=octocat` | `author=[REDACTED]` | `SECRET:context` 0.95 |
| `"author": "Some Name"` | `"author": "[REDACTED]"` | `SECRET:context` |
| `authored_by: bot` | `authored_by: [REDACTED]` | `SECRET:context` |
| `commit 1a2b3c4\nAuthor: github-actions[bot] <…noreply…>` | `Author: [REDACTED] <…>` | `SECRET:context` |
| `Date:   Wed Oct 7 12:00:00 2026 +0300` (git log) | `Date:   [REDACTED]` | `DATE:catalog/azure` 0.95 |
| `Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 12:00:00 GMT` (HTTP) | `Date: [REDACTED]` | `DATE:catalog/azure` |
| `Date: 2026-10-07` | `Date: [REDACTED]` | `DATE:catalog/azure` |

`created: 2026-10-07T12:00:00Z` is correctly kept. So the issue is the `Date` label in the Azure catalog rule, not date parsing.

## Expected

- Credential key affixes must match on word boundaries: `auth`, `auth_token`, `x-auth`, `authorization` yes; `author`, `authored`, `authority`, `authorize_url` no. Add negatives for each.
- A person's name after `Author:` may still be `PERSON` through the name rules (and `Jane Roe` already is). It must not be a credential.
- A generic `DATE` (catalog) finding must not redact by itself. Only `DATE_OF_BIRTH` (or other dates with personal context) should redact by default, as #6 specified. Add git-log, HTTP-header and email-header fixtures as negatives.

title: False positives: bare timestamps and order ids redacted as INN/NHS/NPI/credit card with VERY_LIKELY confidence
body:
## Summary

Since PR #14, the default engine redacts ordinary numbers in logs that have no identity context. Bare checksum rules (`RU_INN`, `UK_NHS`, `US_HEALTHCARE_NPI`) and the Luhn card rule fire on Unix timestamps, millisecond timestamps and order ids. They also report them as `VERY_LIKELY`. AI session logs and CI logs contain these numbers on almost every line, so a large part of the output is destroyed. In non-structured mode, a JSON number also becomes the string marker, so `{"timestamp":[REDACTED]}` is no longer valid JSON.

This conflicts with #11, which asked for "Presidio-style confidence tiers (low without context, high with context or checksum)", and with #4, which asked for "numbers next to unrelated digits (timestamps, version numbers, phone numbers) to keep false positives measured".

## Reproduction (main @ 2306fda, `createSanitizer({})`)

| Input | Output | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| `ts=1696023757` | `ts=[REDACTED]` | `US_HEALTHCARE_NPI:entity-format` 0.85 LIKELY |
| `ts=1696087109` | `ts=[REDACTED]` | `RU_INN:national-format` **0.99 VERY_LIKELY** |
| `ts=1696110866` | `ts=[REDACTED]` | `UK_NHS:national-format` **0.99 VERY_LIKELY** |
| `{"timestamp":1696023757}` | `{"timestamp":[REDACTED]}` (invalid JSON) | NPI |
| `elapsed 1696000628374` | `elapsed [REDACTED]` | `CREDIT_CARD:luhn` (13 digits starting with `1`; no card network uses that prefix) |
| `order 1015032381` | `order [REDACTED]` | `RU_INN` |
| `gọi 090 123 4567` (Vietnamese phone) | redacted, but typed as `UK_NHS` | wrong type |

Measured on 400 generated values each (no identity context anywhere):

| Shape | Redacted |
|---|---|
| `ts=<10-digit Unix seconds>` | 105/400 (26%) |
| `order <10 digits>` | 96/400 (24%) |
| `elapsed <13-digit ms timestamp>` | 37/400 (9%) |
| `run <13 digits>` | 34/400 |
| `id <11 digits>` | 14/400 |

These rates match chance: one check digit passes about 1 in 10 random numbers, and mod-11 about 1 in 11.

## Expected

1. Checksum-only matches without context get low confidence (≈0.3–0.4, `UNLIKELY`/`POSSIBLE`), as in Presidio. A context word in a window (`ИНН`, `NHS`, `NPI`, `SNILS`, `patient`, …) raises it to high.
2. A `minConfidence` / `threshold` option, defaulting to a value that does not redact bare low-confidence checksum matches. A strict publication preset can still lower it explicitly.
3. Credit cards require a valid IIN/network prefix and length (Visa 4 / 13,16,19; Mastercard 51–55, 2221–2720; Amex 34/37 / 15; Discover, JCB, UnionPay, Mir 2200–2204, …), not Luhn alone.
4. Numbers in known timestamp contexts (`timestamp`, `ts`, `time`, `created_at`, `elapsed`, `duration`, `ms`, epoch range 2000–2100) are negatives.
5. Phone numbers that also pass NHS mod-11 are typed `PHONE` when phone context or a trunk prefix is present.
6. Add a regression corpus of realistic log/session lines (timestamps, ids, sizes, ports, PIDs, line:col) with a measured false-positive rate checked in CI.

title: feat: protect identity data and sanitize structured sessions
body:
Sanitized coding sessions previously retained passport MRZs and several document/contact formats, failed on ordinary encoded runs longer than 8,192 characters, and redacted tool metadata needed by session converters. This PR implements all ten child issues together: shared identity and credential detection, explicit masking/fake policies, and JSON/JSONL sanitization with bounded batching and audited encoded fallback.

The [complete requirements, alternatives, implementation plans and primary research](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-13-ae4189325e07/docs/case-studies/repository-issue-13/REQUIREMENTS.md) enumerate every requirement. The [investigation and reproducible experiments](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-13-ae4189325e07/docs/case-studies/repository-issue-13/README.md) preserve root causes, test evidence and measured performance; original issue descriptions/comments are archived alongside them.

### Delivered behavior

| Issue | Implementation and verification |
| --- | --- |
| #3 | Tolerant TD1/TD2/TD3/MRV-A/MRV-B MRZ header/name/data detection, standalone truncated/OCR/reflowed/JSON-escaped fragments, and 7-3-1 confidence scoring. Invalid checks still redact; filler/code/base64 negatives and residual-blocking tests are included. |
| #4 | Unlabelled RU domestic/international and US/UK/DE/IN/KR/IT passport shapes, ICAO document/check digits, multilingual context, confidence tiers, and numeric/identifier boundaries. |
| #5 | Contextual PNR/booking/record locator, 13-digit e-ticket and visa/e-visa references with personal value spans; placeholder words and unrelated git SHAs remain negative. |
| #6 | Short-window multilingual birth vocabulary and slash/dot/ISO/English/Russian month dates, including backticks. Ordinary dates remain unchanged. |
| #7 | Fixed mask `marker`, `minLength`, and `identityMask` preset: first/last two Unicode characters with `***`, full redaction below five. Existing explicit type transforms retain precedence; verification uses full redaction. |
| #8 | Opt-in value-only ICAO/national specimen and repeated/consecutive-digit policies, independent reviewed `fakeValues`, and `kept: 'fake'` auditing. Context words do not exempt values. Real overlapping identities veto automatic specimen exemptions; credentials override every exemption. The same policy runs during residual and decoded-engine checks. |
| #9 | Long encoded runs receive bounded UTF-8 probes and auditable whole-run `ENCODED_LIMIT` fallback. JSON/JSONL scans string keys/values in batches, maps original offsets, verifies parseability and rejects key collisions. Explicit structural fields retain tool metadata while strong credentials/known personal values remain protected. Library, CLI, streams, bounded workers, outbound integration and session example are covered. |
| #10 | Native single/multiline netrc triplets, NuGet `oy2` keys, all eight WordPress KEY/SALT values, and complete PuTTY v3 blocks. Stream boundaries hold multiline credentials together, including one-character chunks/tiny batches. Placeholder negatives retain known-secret priority. |
| #11 | NHS, RRN, codice fiscale, NRIC/FIN, PESEL, personnummer, SA ID, TFN, SIN, formatted SNILS and 10/12-digit INN with common labels, public arithmetic checks, country fixtures and confidence tiers. |
| #12 | All eight requested messenger contexts and Russian call-to-action words, RU/VN/TH/ID national trunk formats with spaces/dashes/parentheses and pipe-separated fields; call/thread IDs and timestamps remain negative. |

Already-covered behavior was retained and regression-tested: explicit UK/Spanish passport labels, structured Russian DOBs, international messenger phones, empty DB_PASSWORD values, required external-engine verification and atomic publication. No listed issue is deferred. Shared changes also update public declarations, documentation and examples. Existing Secretlint/Gitleaks integrations remain enabled by default; no runtime dependency was added.

Research compared ICAO specifications and `cheminfo/mrz`, Presidio recognizers, Nosey Parker rules, PuTTY's PPK specification, `libphonenumber-js`, `python-stdnum` and SNILS validators. Strict parsers alone miss damaged log fragments; Python/Ruby validators do not locate JavaScript text spans. Bounded native rules supplement the existing optional bridges and scanner union. Checksums influence confidence and do not verify issuance.

### Reproduction and validation

Baseline passed 786 tests; running the initial new identity suite against archived baseline source reproduced 72 failures. The four new suites now contain 210 regressions covering the original reproductions, country/layout boundaries, policy conflicts, structured publication and credential records.

```sh
node --test --test-timeout=30000 tests/sanitizer-identity.test.js tests/sanitizer-identity-boundaries.test.js tests/sanitizer-session-identity.test.js tests/sanitizer-credential-formats.test.js
npm test
bun test --timeout 30000
deno test --allow-read --allow-env
npm ci
npm run check
npm run check:secrets
```

Local validation: Node and Bun **996 passed** each; Deno **851 passed**, with existing restricted-permission conventions for process/file integration checks. Strict lint on changed JavaScript, formatting, duplication, secrets, syntax, line limits, required docs, version and one-Changeset guards pass. A minor Changeset prepares the release without manual version changes.

The finite 300-record/56,289-byte benchmark measured 3,269 ms per-value versus 2,448 ms batched (**1.34×**) with required detection and residual verification. A 40,000-string JSON array completed under a 256 MiB heap/512 KiB stack at approximately 133 MiB RSS. These are local measurements, not a throughput guarantee. Oversized textual encodings are conservatively redacted; non-text opaque runs and other existing resource limits retain their documented behavior.

The first published head passed workflow jobs but failed the separate CodeQL alert check on three new backtracking patterns. Both JSON lexical passes now use a deterministic character scanner, and netrc reads its password capture directly. A bounded experiment reproduces the old regex slowdown; an automated regression reproduces the netrc hostname/placeholder bug before the fix. The investigation records the exact check SHA/timestamp, downloaded logs and alert locations. All three flagged expressions were removed without query exclusions or alert dismissals.

### Published verification

Commit `8beb27e16826810347b67b808094805ce0b40c5b` passes all checks. [Checks and release](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/37768985892) includes all nine Node/Bun/Deno × Linux/macOS/Windows combinations; [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/37768985946), [Example app](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/37768985877) and [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/37768985865) also pass. title: Detect national-format phone numbers after messenger labels (WhatsApp, Zalo) and in Russian prose
body:
## Summary

National-format phone numbers without a `+` country code are missed after messenger labels and in Russian prose. A real publication of sanitized sessions exposed about 10 contact numbers from scraped rental advertisements this way. The Telegram handle on the same line was redacted, but the WhatsApp and Zalo numbers next to it were not.

## Reproduction (synthetic numbers)

```js
const s = createSanitizer();
for (const t of [
  'Telegram: @rent_agent_x | WhatsApp: 8 912 555 0142\nZalo: 090 123 4567',
  'Сергей, звоните 8 912 555 0142',
]) console.log((await s.sanitize(t)).text);
// => Telegram: [REDACTED] | WhatsApp: 8 912 555 0142\nZalo: 090 123 4567
// => Сергей, звоните 8 912 555 0142
```

By contrast, `WhatsApp: +7 912 555-01-42`, `Zalo: +84 90 123 4567` and `тел. 8 (912) 555-01-42` are detected.

## Expected

- Messenger labels (WhatsApp, Zalo, Viber, Telegram, Signal, WeChat, LINE, KakaoTalk) count as phone context, also when several `label: value` pairs share one line separated by `|`.
- National trunk-prefix formats: Russia `8 9xx xxx xxxx`, Vietnam `0[35789]x xxx xxxx`, Thailand `0x xxx xxxx`, Indonesia `08xx xxxx xxxx`, with space, dash and parenthesis grouping.
- Russian imperative call-to-action context (звоните, пишите, звонить, номер телефона) as context words.
- Negatives: tool-call ids such as `call_<digits>…`, thread ids in test output, and timestamps.

title: National identifiers without short labels: NHS, RRN, codice fiscale, NRIC, PESEL, personnummer, SA ID, TFN, SIN, SNILS, INN
body:
## Summary

National identifiers that competitors test are only reachable through long catalog names, not through common short labels or format rules. All probes used synthetic values.

- UK NHS number (10 digits with mod-11 check) without a label.
- Korean RRN, Italian codice fiscale, Singapore NRIC/FIN, Polish PESEL, Swedish personnummer with common short labels (`RRN`, `CF`, `NRIC`, `PESEL`, `personnummer`).
- South African ID (13 digits with Luhn).
- Australian TFN and Canadian SIN short labels (`TFN`, `SIN`).
- Russian SNILS (`ddd-ddd-ddd dd` with checksum) and INN (10/12 digits with checksum) without labels. With a `snils`/`inn` label both are detected; bare values such as `112-233-445 95` are not.

## Expected

Format rules with checksum validation where public algorithms exist, Presidio-style confidence tiers (low without context, high with context or checksum), and fixtures per country.

title: Missing credential formats found in competitor test suites: .netrc, NuGet, WordPress keys/salts, PuTTY v3
body:
## Summary

A comparison against competitor test suites (noseyparker, gitleaks HEAD, trufflehog, detect-secrets, secretlint) found credential formats that are missed. All probes used synthetic values.

| Format | Example (synthetic) | Covered by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.netrc` credentials | `machine api.example.net login alice password Zq8vR2mT9xLp` | noseyparker `np.netrc.1` |
| NuGet API key | `oy2` + 43 lowercase alphanumerics | noseyparker `np.nuget.1` (gitleaks rule is limited to `nuget.config` paths) |
| WordPress keys and salts in `define()` | `define('AUTH_KEY', 'q8Zv#R2m!T9xLp@Q7nWc4bY6dF1hJ0kS');`, also `SECURE_AUTH_KEY`, `LOGGED_IN_KEY`, `NONCE_KEY`, `*_SALT` (`DB_PASSWORD` is already detected) | noseyparker, ggshield |
| PuTTY v3 private key | a complete `PuTTY-User-Key-File-3:` block including `Private-Lines` and `Private-MAC` is returned unchanged | gitleaks matches only `File-2` |

## Expected

The `.netrc` triplet is missed both on one line and across lines. Detect each format with complete-span redaction, plus negatives for placeholders (`password ${PASS}`, `define('DB_PASSWORD', '')`, `example.com`). The vendored gitleaks rule set is current (222 rules at HEAD), so these need native rules.

title: Session JSONL sanitization fails with ERR_LIMIT and redacts JSON structure (tool names, ids)
body:
## Summary

Sanitizing AI session logs (Claude Code / Codex JSONL) with the documented APIs is not practical today:

1. `sanitize()` / `sanitizeStream()` / the `redact --stream` CLI fail with `ERR_LIMIT` on ordinary records. The encoded-run scanner throws when a percent-encoded run or a wrapped base64 block exceeds 8192 characters, and session logs contain long URLs and base64 tool outputs.
2. On JSON text the engine redacts structural values: tool names (`"name":"Read"` as `PERSON`), message/request/tool-call ids (`toolu_…`, `req_…`, `msg_…` as `SECRET`), and whole skill descriptions as `SECRET context`. This makes the output useless for conversion tools that rely on these fields.

## Reproduction (synthetic data)

```js
const s = createSanitizer();
await s.sanitize(JSON.stringify({ url: 'https://example.org/search?q=' + 'word%20'.repeat(2000) })); // throws ERR_LIMIT
await s.sanitize('A'.repeat(100) + ('\n' + 'B'.repeat(100)).repeat(120));                       // throws ERR_LIMIT
const r = await s.sanitize(JSON.stringify({ type: 'tool_use', id: 'toolu_01CM9SwFYXq3vJ6cjYAFFjkf', name: 'Read' }));
// => {"type":"tool_use","id":"[REDACTED]","name":"[REDACTED]"}
```

## Expected

- An over-long encoded run should not block the whole input. Decode it in bounded windows, or fall back to non-decoded detection for that run, and report it as a finding.
- A JSON/JSONL-aware mode, for example `sanitizeJsonl()` or `structured: 'json'`, that sanitizes string values and keys separately, keeps the document parseable, and lets callers declare structural fields (ids, tool names, types) as non-personal.
- Performance: the current engine processes about 0.1–0.4 MB/s, so a 750 MB session takes hours. Batching or worker parallelism inside the library would help.

Workaround used downstream: walk every JSON string value, batch values with a separator, and fall back to `decode: false` on `ERR_LIMIT`.

title: Allow explicitly fake identity data (specimens, synthetic numbers, reviewed allowlist) but never by context words
body:
## Summary

Allow explicitly fake identity data, such as test fixtures and documentation specimens, while redacting everything else. Today a project cannot tell the sanitizer "this passport line is a known fake", so it has to choose between over-redacting test fixtures and leaking real data.

## Proposal

A value is treated as explicitly fake only when one of these holds:

1. It is an official specimen: ICAO Doc 9303 specimen data (issuing state `UTO`, `ERIKSSON<<ANNA<MARIA`, document numbers such as `L898902C3`), national specimen markers (`SPECIMEN`, `ОБРАЗЕЦ`, `MUSTERMANN`).
2. It is obviously synthetic: one repeated digit, or 6 or more consecutive ascending or descending digits in the document number (`123456`, `987654`).
3. It is listed in a reviewed allowlist supplied by the caller (`fakeValues: [...]`), which is kept outside the published data.

Context words like "test", "fake" or "example" next to the value must NOT be enough. In the real leak that prompted this issue, real passport data appeared inside tests and messages such as "real-data tests".

## Expected

- Option `fakeIdentity: 'specimen-and-synthetic'` (default off for credentials, recommended on for identity documents).
- Findings for kept fake values are reported with `kept: 'fake'`, so audits can count them.
- Residual verification ignores only values that pass the same fake check.

## Tests

ICAO specimen TD3 lines kept; `9876543217RUS9001014F300101...` kept (descending document number); a realistic synthetic number such as `5839204716RUS...` redacted even when the line says "test passport".

title: Identity masking transformation: keep 2+2 characters with *** and fully redact values shorter than 5
Detect dates of birth in natural language and loose labels
body:
## Summary

Dates of birth are detected only with a structured key such as `dob: ...`. Natural-language and loosely labelled birth dates pass through. A real leak included remarks like "real DOB `02/03/1990`".

## Reproduction (synthetic data)

```js
const s = createSanitizer();
for (const t of [
  'she was born on 07/12/1985 in Kazan',
  'All correct - real DOB `02/03/1990`',
  'birth date 1985-12-07',
]) console.log((await s.sanitize(t)).text);
// None are redacted. 'Дата рождения: 07.12.1985' is detected, so the gap is label coverage, not date parsing.
```

## Expected

- `DATE_OF_BIRTH` when birth vocabulary (born, birth date, DOB, дата рождения, д.р., родился/родилась, Geburtsdatum, fecha de nacimiento, date de naissance) appears within a short window before a date, including markdown/backtick quoting.
- All common date shapes: `dd/mm/yyyy`, `mm/dd/yyyy`, `dd.mm.yyyy`, ISO, and month names in English and Russian.
- Keep plain dates (commit dates, timestamps) untouched without birth context.

title: Detect travel booking data: PNR/booking references, e-ticket and visa numbers
body:
## Summary

Travel booking data is not detected: airline booking references (PNR / record locator), e-ticket numbers and visa or e-visa application numbers. In a real leak, a booking reference and airline notification identifiers were published from sanitized sessions.

## Reproduction (synthetic data)

```js
const s = createSanitizer();
for (const t of [
  'booking reference K7QWZP',
  'PNR: XKJHQZ, record locator XKJHQZ',
  'код брони K7QWZP',
  'e-ticket 098-2401234567',
  'e-visa registration code E260512ABCDEF',
]) console.log((await s.sanitize(t)).text);
// None are redacted.
```

## Expected

- `BOOKING_REFERENCE`: 5–8 alphanumeric characters after context words (booking reference/code, reservation code, confirmation code, record locator, PNR, код брони, номер брони, бронирование).
- `TICKET_NUMBER`: 13-digit IATA e-ticket numbers (3-digit airline prefix + 10 digits) with context.
- `VISA_NUMBER`: visa / e-visa / registration numbers after context words.
- Personal category, so masking transformations apply.

## Tests

Negatives must include ordinary uppercase words after "booking" (for example `booking reference: NONE`) and git short SHAs.

title: Detect passport numbers without explicit labels (Russian domestic/international and country formats)
body:
## Summary

Passport numbers are only detected when they follow an explicit label such as `паспорт:`. Formats commonly found in logs and AI sessions without such a label are missed. This contributed to a real leak of passport data.

## Reproduction (synthetic data)

```js
const s = createSanitizer();
for (const t of [
  'series and number: 45 17 839204',          // RU domestic passport
  '4517 839204',                              // RU domestic, compact
  'загран 75 4930281',                        // RU international passport
]) console.log((await s.sanitize(t)).text);
// None are redacted. (By contrast, 'UK passport 123456789' and 'pasaporte AB1234567' are detected.)
```

## Expected

- Russian domestic passport `dd dd dddddd` / `dddd dddddd` and international `dd ddddddd` as format rules, with higher confidence when Russian/English passport vocabulary appears within a window (not only as a `key: value` label).
- Country formats with validation where public algorithms exist (ICAO 9-character document numbers with check digit, US 9 digits, UK 9 digits, DE `[CFGHJK][0-9CFGHJKLMNPRTVWXYZ]{8}`, IN `[A-Z][0-9]{7}`, KR `M[0-9]{3}[A-Z][0-9]{4}`, IT `[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{7}`), using a Presidio-style confidence model: low score without context, high with context or checksum.
- Multilingual context vocabulary: passport, паспорт, загранпаспорт, серия, номер, pasaporte, Reisepass, passeport, passaporto, 护照, パスポート.

## Tests

Positive and negative fixtures per country, including numbers next to unrelated digits (timestamps, version numbers, phone numbers) to keep false positives measured.

title: Detect passport machine-readable zones (ICAO 9303 MRZ): real passport data leaked
body:
## Summary

Passport machine-readable zones (ICAO Doc 9303 MRZ) are not detected at all. In a real publication of sanitized AI coding sessions, several MRZ lines of real passports passed through `createSanitizer().sanitize()` unchanged and became public. The data was contained, but passport data is critical personal data and must never pass.

## Reproduction (synthetic data)

```js
import { createSanitizer } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const s = createSanitizer();
console.log((await s.sanitize(
  'mrz: P<RUSKOVALEVA<<MARINA<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<\n5839204716RUS8204117M310519<<<<<<<<<<<<<<02'
)).text);
// Both lines are returned unchanged, even with the "mrz:" label.
```

## Expected

Detect all ICAO 9303 MRZ formats regardless of context:

- TD3 (passports, 2 x 44 characters), TD2 (2 x 36), TD1 (ID cards, 3 x 30), MRV-A/MRV-B visas.
- The name line (`P<`, `I<`, `A<`, `C<`, `V<` + issuing state + names with `<` fillers).
- The data line, also when only a fragment is present (document number + check digit + nationality + birth date + check digit + sex + expiry + check digit). Real logs often contain a truncated or reflowed line.
- Validate check digits (7-3-1 weights) to raise confidence, but do NOT require valid check digits to redact: a typo in a real MRZ is still personal data.
- New types such as `PASSPORT_MRZ`, category `personal`.

## Tests

- Positive: synthetic TD1/TD2/TD3 lines with valid and invalid check digits; line fragments; MRZ embedded in JSON strings with `\n` escapes; lowercase-free OCR variants with spaces between groups.
- Negative: long runs of `<` alone, base64 strings, C++ templates like `vector<<int>>`.
- Residual verification must fail if an MRZ survives.

Competitors: no open tool has a complete MRZ detector (Presidio only touches TD1 inside the German ID recognizer), so this would be a real differentiator.

title: feat: sanitize multilingual sensitive data and add safe publication tools
body:
Fixes #1.

Adds an offline sensitive-text library, detector framework and CLI for logs, files and AI sessions, and addresses the requirements review in this PR. Credentials are fully redacted by default; publication fails when a required detector fails, a limit is exceeded, or verification finds a residual.

The previous parser leaked credential suffixes: `Password: Tr0ub4dor&3` retained `&3`, prose values stopped at spaces, and escaped JSON quotes ended the value early. Context-specific boundaries now cover complete quoted, prose/YAML, query and shell values. All 26 named review examples failed at `60cdd96` before implementation and now pass with the default async engine.

### Delivered behavior

- Required Secretlint plus **221 bundled Gitleaks 8.30.1 text rules**, compiled with RE2/WASM, pinned provenance/licenses and a reproducible sync script. Native entropy, checksum/format validators, contextual credentials, known command flags and bounded Unicode/encoded views supplement the union.
- Default free-text name recognition in **17 locales**, national phones/IDs, addresses, IBAN, handles, MACs and home-path usernames. Expanded prose/inflected labels and non-Latin digits retain original UTF-16 spans.
- Offline sourced public knowledge and role/domain heuristics, reviewed custom policies and opt-in Wikidata lookup. Credentials and explicit private values take priority; private dictionary overlaps are never submitted for public verification.
- Native Google/Azure/AWS catalog labels (213/176/36), typed confidence/likelihood and optional masks, keyed pseudonyms, character-shape pseudonyms, date shifting and bucketing. Full masking remains the default. HTML/byte/JSON decoding, optional re-encoding and Hive-compatible masks are supported.
- Bounded record streaming and file workers, private atomic publication, optional local `gh auth` values, outbound/Sentry helpers and an ESLint publication-boundary rule. Late invalid UTF-8 and timed-out workers leave no published file or staging directory.
- `history rewrite` previews private replacement/mailmap plans in a fresh mirror clone. Explicit `--apply` runs git-filter-repo only on that clone, redacts blobs/messages/identities/paths/refs, re-audits and removes private plans. It never pushes or changes the source repository.
- Template arithmetic, CLI and historical documents move to explicit legacy entries. Arithmetic behavior and the universal app remain available; Changesets prepare the next minor release.

### Validation

**Node: 786 passed. Bun: 786 passed. Deno: 641 passed (8 steps).** Filesystem/subprocess integration runs under Node/Bun; Deno exercises the library with the existing read/environment permissions.

Lint, formatting, duplication, Secretlint, workflow policy, syntax, declaration and tracked-file line-limit checks pass. The packed archive installs and runs the sanitizer API/CLI and legacy CLI; the Vite app builds. Actual git-filter-repo 2.47.0 integration verifies deleted historical secrets, messages, identities, filenames, a clean post-rewrite audit, an unchanged source HEAD and a clone without a remote. Finite heap/stack probes and every UTF-8 split boundary are covered. [Reproduction and validation](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-1-b188f503edf3/docs/case-studies/issue-1/VALIDATION.md).

The independently executed [comparison](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-1-b188f503edf3/experiments/benchmark/README.md) commits **223 synthetic cases / 210 annotated spans**, pinned versions/settings, raw predictions and corpus/source fingerprints. Full-span recall: sanitizer 100%, Gitleaks 1.43%, TruffleHog 1.43%, detect-secrets 12.38%, Presidio 41.43%, scrubadub 11.43%. The default sanitizer had no false predictions on this development corpus. It is not held out; labelled multilingual cases favor contextual detectors, English PII and secret-only baselines have different scopes, and overlap precision does not measure excess redaction. Proprietary services were not executed.

### Research and practical limits

The [case study](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-1-b188f503edf3/docs/case-studies/issue-1/README.md) preserves paginated inventories of 1,733 accessible owned repositories, indexed searches, primary documentation, source hashes and related PRs. The [review matrix](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-1-b188f503edf3/docs/case-studies/issue-1/REVIEW-FOLLOWUP.md) maps the requested follow-up to code and tests, including Hive streaming, decoding, masking, auth and publication practices.

The default gazetteer and national-format grammars have finite coverage. Catalog-label recognition does not reproduce proprietary NLP; shape pseudonyms are not NIST FF1 encryption, and optional partial transforms retain information. Online name matches do not prove identity. Compression/OCR, undisclosed models and remote history/cache erasure remain outside this text implementation. [API and limits](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-1-b188f503edf3/docs/COVERAGE.md).

The first follow-up CI exposed the one-Changeset-per-PR requirement and a CodeQL polynomial-regex alert. Saved logs and a bounded failing regression led to consolidated release notes and a whitespace-boundary fix; the 128 KiB-tab probe now completes in about 4 ms. A later Windows Bun failure was isolated to the synchronous child wrapper. Asynchronous execution passes with the same two-second deadline, heap/stack limits and a separate matching-time assertion: saved Windows job log line 811 records the regression passing in 610 ms; lines 1305–1308 record 749 tests passing with zero failures. The exact upstream process-wrapper cause is not established.

title: Collect all best practices we used to do sanitation of sensitive data from our projects

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
Check our all our organizations repositories:
- link-foundation
- linksplatform
- link-assistant
- konard (user)

For example:
- github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind
- github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai
- github.com/konard/documents-processing

Collect all logic and best practices we used for sanitation, and make sure we implement the most robust framework/library and cli on a the market to fully sanitize any text files like logs, AI sessions and so on.

We should be able to do sanitation of personal data (names, emails and so), but we should be able to do it smartly - if that includes some public popular people and public organizations and for example email was made public on the internet by organization itself we should be able to treat such data as not personal.

And all credentials (tokens, passwords and so on), which are clear from context.

The most important feature for this system is reliability so it must use all algorithms from competitors, or reimplement a more advanced algorithms here, so we bet exactly all open-source competitors in the field, and provide best possible sanitation for sensitive data on the market.

For closed source competitors we should use their docs and examples to support all their features as well.

We may also include tools to carefully redact / edit history of GitHub, to make sure sensitive data was removed from the history.

We should support as much natural languages as possible, and work with all their specifics. And as much popular services as possible where the format of credential tokens is known.

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
